# Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its APD-licensed Group Home Facility in Florida. The home provides Residential Habilitation under the iBudget Florida waiver and is licensed under Chapter 393, F.S., and Chapter 65G-2, F.A.C. The manual is meant to:

- Turn the licensing, staffing, resident-care, emergency, medication, screening and Medicaid waiver requirements that apply to the home into clear, usable procedures.
- Protect the health, safety, dignity, rights and choices of the people who live in the home.
- Give owners, the facility operator, managers and direct service professionals (DSPs) one consistent reference for daily practice, so that expectations are the same on every shift.
- Help [AGENCY NAME] show compliance during APD monitoring, license renewal, Medicaid reviews and incident follow-up.

## Customization, adoption, currency and training

This manual is a template. It is not in force until [AGENCY NAME] completes each step below.

1. **Customize it.** Replace every [AGENCY NAME] placeholder and every other bracketed field (facility name, license number, address, licensed capacity, resident characteristics, regional office, names and titles, phone numbers) with accurate local information. Revise the procedures to match how each home actually operates. Each home has its own license, so make home-specific entries where they differ.
2. **Have the governing body adopt it.** The owner, board of directors or other governing body must formally adopt the manual. Record the adoption date and the approving signatures on the adoption page. Record every later revision the same way.
3. **Keep it current.** Rules change. Chapter 65G-2, F.A.C., was amended and parts of it were repealed effective 3/26/2026. Review the manual at least annually, and whenever a rule, statute, handbook, rate table or APD directive changes. Keep a revision log, and keep superseded versions on file.
4. **Train all staff on it.** Every employee must be trained on the manual and on any revision before working independently. Keep signed acknowledgments and training records. This is in addition to the training Florida rules require, such as Zero Tolerance, CPR/first aid, medication administration, the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) and behavior-plan training.

> This manual is an operational aid. It is not legal advice and does not replace the full text of the governing statutes and rules. If anything in this manual conflicts with a current statute, rule or APD/AHCA directive, the statute, rule or directive controls. Have the manual reviewed by qualified counsel or a compliance professional before adoption.

# How to Use This Manual

## Who must use it

The manual applies to the owner/licensee, the facility operator and backup operator, managers and supervisors, DSPs, relief and temporary staff, and anyone else who works in the home or has access to residents, their funds or their property.

## Before you start

1. **Search for every bracketed placeholder**, such as [AGENCY NAME], and complete it. Do not distribute a version that still has blank fields.
2. **Check each cited rule against the current official text.** Use the links in the Regulatory Framework section. Several citations carry specific cautions:
   - Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C. (Reactive Strategies): the text cited is the 2008 adoption, and APD has draft revisions in development.
   - Chapter 65G-4, F.A.C.: the text cited is the 4/4/2012 rule.
   - s. 393.13, F.S.: confirm the subsection numbering against the current statute.
   - Rule 65G-2.0021, 65G-2.004, 65G-2.0041 and 65G-2.005, F.A.C.: titles and effective dates are verified, but you should read the full rule text before writing detailed procedures.
   - Rule 59G-13.081, F.A.C.: a July 2026 rate table is in rule development, so confirm which table is in effect before using any rate.
3. **Match the manual to your license.** Serve only residents whose characteristics match the home's license, and keep the licensed capacity and census entries accurate.

## Suggested working method

- **New employees:** Read the whole manual during orientation. Sign the acknowledgment page, and complete the required trainings within the deadlines set by rule.
- **Daily practice:** Use the table of contents to find the procedure for the situation you are in. Examples are an incident, a medication question, a fire drill, a resident-funds transaction or a schedule change.
- **Emergencies and reporting:** Keep the emergency and reporting procedures, including the Abuse Hotline number, where every staff member can reach them. Rule 65G-2.010 requires emergency numbers at every phone extension.
- **Supervisors:** Use the manual for supervision, performance evaluations, record audits and corrective action.
- **Preparing for monitoring or renewal:** Use the manual as a checklist against APD monitoring, which occurs at least monthly, and against license renewal.

## Organization of the manual

The sections that follow this front matter cover licensure and administration, physical plant and siting, staffing and training, resident care, rights and behavior supports, medication, emergency and incident procedures, finances, and Medicaid waiver service delivery. Each procedure should cite the rule or statute it implements. When a requirement is revised, update the procedure and the citation together.

## Records and acknowledgment

Keep the adoption record, the revision log, the staff acknowledgments and the training records on file, in the office area with secure records storage. Retain each record for the period the applicable rule requires.

# Regulatory Framework

The rules and statutes below govern the Group Home Facility. Citations appear exactly as given. Obtain and read the current official text of each one before relying on this summary.

## Facility licensure and administration

- **s. 393.067, F.S.** (Facility licensure): APD licenses group home facilities (4-15 residents) and foster care facilities (3 or fewer). The statute requires Level 2 screening, proof of financial ability, a comprehensive emergency management plan and an annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients. APD cannot fund an unlicensed facility.
- **s. 393.063, F.S.** (Definitions): a foster care facility has 3 or fewer residents, and a group home facility has 4-15 residents. No new residential habilitation centers are licensed.
- **Rule 65G-2.002, F.A.C.** (License Application and Renewal Procedures): each home has its own license. Renewals are due at least 45 days before expiration. Late or incomplete renewals are treated as initial applications. APD must receive 30 days' written notice before a home closes.
- **Rule 65G-2.003, F.A.C.** (Length of Licenses): residential facility licenses are issued for one year.
- **Rule 65G-2.0032, F.A.C.** (Agency Monitoring and Oversight): APD monitors licensed homes at least monthly, including one weekend visit a year. It may request proof of ability to operate 60 days without state payment, and it reviews the home on site within 30 days after the first admission.
- **Rule 65G-2.006, F.A.C.** (Licensed Residential Facility Capacity): APD sets licensed capacity and resident characteristics. Capacity changes require 30 days' notice, a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance. Census changes must be reported in writing.
- **Rules 65G-2.0021, 65G-2.004, 65G-2.0041, 65G-2.005, F.A.C.** (Change of Ownership; License Violations, non-disciplinary and disciplinary; License Denial, Suspension or Revocation): effective 3/26/2026. Chapter 65G-2 also repealed 65G-2.017 (Health Safety Standards) and 65G-2.014 effective 3/26/2026.

## Physical plant and siting

- **Rule 65G-2.007, F.A.C.** (General Residential Facility Standards): bedroom and bathroom ratios, living space, water temperature, detectors, hazard controls, meals, and an office area with secure records storage.
- **Rule 65G-2.0072, F.A.C.** (Group Home Facility Standards): facility operator qualifications, on-site or on-call availability with a designated backup, and a designated office area.
- **Rule 65G-2.015, F.A.C.; s. 419.001, F.S.** (Siting; site selection of community residential homes): limits on the number of APD facilities within 1,000 ft, zoning treatment by home size, the 60-day local government review for homes of 7-14 residents, and zoning notice at the first resident.
- **42 CFR 441.301(c)** (HCBS settings requirements): provider-owned or controlled residential settings need a lease or equivalent agreement, lockable bedroom doors, roommate choice, access to food and visitors, freedom to decorate, and documented person-centered justification for any modification.

## Staffing, screening and training

- **Rule 65G-2.008, F.A.C.** (Staffing Requirements for Residential Facilities): adequate staffing, DSP qualifications, fitness for duty, driver standards, FDLE sexual offender/predator database checks, personnel records, schedules, and training requirements (core competencies, CPR/first aid, Zero Tolerance, HIV/AIDS, behavior-plan training, and Ch. 65G-8 compliance).
- **s. 393.0655, F.S.** (Screening of direct service providers): Level 2 employment screening under ch. 435 for direct service providers, managers, supervisors and anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property.
- **s. 435.12, F.S.** (Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse): screening results are managed through the AHCA Clearinghouse, where employers register and track eligibility.

## Resident care, rights and behavior supports

- **Rule 65G-2.009, F.A.C.** (Resident Care and Supervision Standards): care standards, the Bill of Rights, house rules, community activities, admission and termination, resident funds, resident records, supervision, video monitoring, behavioral interventions, the sexual activity policy and Safety Plan safeguards, first aid, medication, specialized equipment, transportation and staff communication.
- **s. 393.13, F.S.** (Treatment of persons with developmental disabilities, Bill of Rights): rights of all persons with developmental disabilities, including freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation and unnecessary restraint or seclusion. Confirm the current subsection numbering.
- **Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C. (65G-8.001-.012)** (Reactive Strategies): required curriculum, certification, policies, chemical restraint, prohibited procedures, and documentation and notification. Confirm the current text before finalizing.
- **Chapter 65G-4, F.A.C. (65G-4.008, 65G-4.009, 65G-4.010)** (Service Delivery Practice and Procedure - Behavior Analysis Services): certified behavior analyst oversight and Local Review Committee review of written plans. Confirm the current text.

## Medication

- **s. 393.506, F.S.** (Administration of medication): training, validation, annual in-service and revalidation requirements for unlicensed direct service providers.
- **Rule 65G-7.004, F.A.C.** (Medication administration training and validation): the APD Basic Medication Administration course, validation, and annual update and revalidation. Chapter 65G-7 is also incorporated by 65G-2.009(12)(e)-(f) for the daily medication record, storage and error reporting.

## Emergency, incident and abuse reporting

- **Rule 65G-2.010, F.A.C.** (Fire and Emergency Procedures): emergency numbers, annual fire inspection under ch. 69A-38, monthly fire drills, the CEMP, missing residents, and incident reporting (APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006).
- **ss. 39.201 and 415.1034, F.S. (as incorporated by Rule 65G-2.010(6)(a), F.A.C.)** (Mandatory reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation): known or suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873. The citation is verified as it appears in the text of 65G-2.010(6)(a); the statute text was not independently fetched.

## Finances and Medicaid waiver services

- **Rule 65G-2.018, F.A.C.; Rule 65G-13.008, F.A.C.** (Personal Needs Allowance; Room and Board Payment): the personal needs allowance, the APD room-and-board standard, and the claiming deadline using Form 65G-13.008A.
- **Rule 59G-13.070, F.A.C. (iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook, May 2023)**: Residential Habilitation requirements, minimum direct-care hours, billing, provider qualifications, behavior-focus designations, the implementation plan, quarterly summary and annual report. The Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement is AHCA Form 5000-3553.
- **Rule 59G-13.081, F.A.C.** (iBudget Waiver Services Provider Rate Table): rates by support level and county group. The Oct. 1, 2025 table is incorporated. A July 2026 table is in rule development (Notice 31315303).

## Employment

- **s. 448.110, F.S.; Fla. Const. art. X, s. 24** (Florida Minimum Wage): $15.00/hour from Sept. 30, 2026.
- **s. 440.02, F.S.** (Workers' compensation definitions): coverage is required for employers with four or more employees.

## Verification reminder

citations.title: General Residential Facility Standards
citations.requirement: Physical plant standards: no mobile homes; maximum 2 residents per bedroom for homes first licensed on or after 7/1/2014; bedroom space of at least 80 sq ft (single) or 60 sq ft per person (shared); one toilet, sink and tub/shower per 3 residents; 35 sq ft of living/dining space per household member; hot water at or below 120°F; smoke and CO detectors; restricted access to water hazards; secured hazardous chemicals; meal provisions; an office area with secure records storage.

citations.title: Group Home Facility Standards
citations.requirement: The facility operator needs 90 college credits in a related field, or a high school diploma plus 3 years of disability experience. The operator must be on site or on call at all times, with a designated backup (subsecs. (2)-(3)). The home needs a designated office area (subsec. (4)).

citations.title: Staffing Requirements for Residential Facilities (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: The licensee must employ adequate staff for the number and characteristics of residents, even above the minimum (subsec. (1)). DSP qualifications are in subsec. (2): age 18+; ch. 435 / s. 393.0655 screening; high school diploma or equivalent; 1 year of experience or 30 semester hours / 45 quarter hours / 720 classroom hours of related training. Subsec. (2)(f)-(h) sets the supervised 90-day alternative, written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days of hire, and a performance evaluation within 120 days. Subsec. (3) sets required skills. Subsec. (4) covers fitness for duty, driver standards (no qualifying violation in 3 years, annual driving-history update) and the annual FDLE sexual offender/predator database check within one mile. Subsec. (5) covers investigations. Subsec. (6) covers personnel records, job descriptions, weekly schedules posted one week ahead and actual schedules kept 6 months; copies go to APD within 3 calendar days. Subsec. (7) sets training: Direct Care Core Competencies and classroom CPR/first aid within 90 days, Zero Tolerance before services with refresher every 3 years, HIV/AIDS within 90 days, behavior-plan training by a certified behavior analyst, and Ch. 65G-8 compliance. Training records are kept 3 years.

citations.title: Resident Care and Supervision Standards (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Subsec. (1) covers care standards, the Bill of Rights, written house rules and follow-up of medical appointments. Subsec. (2) requires community activity opportunities. Subsec. (3) covers admission/termination criteria, notice to APD before accepting each new resident and a census change report within 5 calendar days. It also covers transfer approval and the property inventory. Subsec. (4) covers resident funds. Subsec. (5) covers resident records: contents, updated within 30 days of new information, retained 6 years, copies to APD within 2 calendar days. Subsec. (6) requires at least one staff present at all times residents are in the facility, with limited exceptions by Regional Office-approved plan. Subsec. (7) covers video monitoring. Subsec. (8) covers behavioral interventions. Subsec. (9) covers the sexual activity policy and Safety Plan safeguards. Subsec. (10) covers solicitation. Subsec. (11) covers first aid. Subsec. (12) covers medication. Subsec. (13) covers specialized equipment. Subsec. (14) covers transportation. Subsec. (15) covers staff communication.

citations.title: Fire and Emergency Procedures (amended 3-26-26)
citations.requirement: Subsec. (1) requires emergency numbers at every phone extension. Subsec. (2) requires an annual fire inspection under ch. 69A-38 and an approved inspection before initial licensure or renewal. Subsec. (3) requires monthly fire drills, with records kept 1 year and no drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m. Subsec. (4) covers the CEMP: reviewed/updated annually, staff trained within 30 days of hire and annually, evacuation reported to the Regional Office within 6 hours and every 6 hours after, emergency shelter over-capacity reported within 48 hours. Subsec. (5) covers missing residents. Subsec. (6) covers incident reporting: Abuse Hotline immediately; APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 (Dec. 2025); initial notice of a critical incident within 4 hours and the completed form within 1 calendar day; reportable incidents within 1 calendar day; follow-up within 5 days.

citations.title: Siting; site selection of community residential homes
citations.requirement: No more than three APD facilities within 1,000 ft (rule subsec. (4)). Homes of 6 or fewer residents are a single-family use. Homes of 7-14 residents must be in multifamily zoning, and local government has 60 days to approve or deny. Notify zoning when the home receives its first resident.

citations.title: Personal Needs Allowance; Room and Board Payment
citations.requirement: The personal needs allowance is at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate ($178.92/month at the 2026 SSI rate of $994). APD room-and-board standard is $583.42/month. Claim room and board on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end.

citations.title: Medication administration training and validation
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff may administer medication only after the APD Basic Medication Administration course (exam of at least 85%; 100% on the MAR section) and validation by an approved validator. They must complete an annual update and revalidation, and revalidate within the 60 days before expiry. Ch. 65G-7 is also incorporated by 65G-2.009(12)(e)-(f) for the daily medication record, storage and error reporting.

citations.title: Administration of medication
citations.requirement: An unlicensed direct service provider may supervise self-administration or administer oral, transdermal, ophthalmic, otic, rectal, inhaled, enteral or topical prescription medications only after an initial course of at least 6 hours by an agency-approved trainer. Validation is onsite with an actual client and medication, initially and annually, for oral, enteral, ophthalmic, rectal and inhaled routes. Otic, transdermal and topical routes are validated by simulation in the initial course. An annual 2-hour in-service on medication administration and error prevention is required. A provider who misses revalidation or the in-service must repeat the initial course. APD must set procedures by rule.

citations.title: Screening of direct service providers
citations.requirement: Level 2 employment screening under ch. 435 is required for direct service providers, managers and supervisors of licensed residential facilities, and anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property. Exemptions from disqualification only as provided in s. 435.07. Disqualifying offenses include those listed in the statute.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Screening results are managed through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse. Employers register and track eligibility there.

citations.title: Treatment of persons with developmental disabilities (Bill of Rights)
citations.requirement: Rights in subsec. (3) apply to all persons with developmental disabilities. They include dignity, privacy and humane care; freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation and unnecessary restraint, isolation or excessive medication; religious freedom; social interaction and community participation; exercise and recreation; the right to consent to or refuse treatment, subject to a guardian advocate (s. 393.12) or guardian (ch. 744); and no discrimination in publicly funded programs. No behavioral program may be implemented unless reviewed under APD rule. Clients have the right to be free from unnecessary restraint or seclusion, and APD adopts rules limiting its use. Confirm the current subsection numbering against the 2025 statute.

citations.title: Reactive Strategies
citations.requirement: Providers that use reactive strategies need an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum (65G-8.002): at least 12 direct training hours, a written test with an 80% minimum score, and certification valid for one year. Staff must be certified before using any technique. 65G-8.003 requires policies and procedures, an annual internal review and consent information in client records. 65G-8.008 covers chemical restraint. 65G-8.009 lists prohibited procedures. 65G-8.010 covers documentation and notification. Cited text is the 2008 adoption; APD has draft revisions in development, so confirm the current text before finalizing.

citations.title: Service Delivery Practice and Procedure - Behavior Analysis Services

Written plans go to the Local Review Committee (LRC) chair within 5 working days after implementation (65G-4.010(1)). The LRC reviews, approves or disapproves plans. Disapproved plans are revised and resubmitted within 14 working days (65G-4.008). Cited text is the 4/4/2012 rule; confirm current text.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Facility Operator/Program Director Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Owner/licensee, governing body, Facility Operator/Program Director, designated backup, and all managers and supervisors of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed, who is accountable for the licensed group home, and what the Facility Operator/Program Director must do so that each home is licensed, adequately staffed and run in compliance with Florida law.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is licensed by the Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD) as a Group Home Facility (4-15 residents) or Foster Care Facility (3 or fewer residents) under s. 393.067, F.S., and Chapter 65G-2, F.A.C. The owner/licensee and governing body are accountable for the operation of every licensed home. Each home must have a qualified Facility Operator who is on site or on call at all times, with a designated backup for any absence. The licensee will employ enough qualified staff for the number and characteristics of residents, even when that is more than the minimum. The governing body will review and approve the annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded residents before it is filed.

definitions.definition: A residential facility licensed by APD that serves 4 to 15 residents (s. 393.063, F.S.).
A residential facility licensed by APD that serves 3 or fewer residents (s. 393.063, F.S.).
The owner or the board or other body that holds the APD license and has final authority and accountability for the agency.
The qualified person responsible for day-to-day operation of the licensed home and compliance with Chapter 65G-2, F.A.C.
A named, qualified person who assumes the Facility Operator's duties when the operator is unavailable.

procedures: The governing body adopts a written organizational chart showing the owner/licensee, governing body, Facility Operator/Program Director, designated backup, supervisors and direct support staff for each licensed home. The Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) updates it whenever a position changes.

Before a person is named Facility Operator, the governing body verifies that the person holds either 90 college credits in a related field or a high school diploma plus 3 years of experience working with people with disabilities. It keeps copies of transcripts or verified experience letters in the personnel file.

Before a person begins as owner/applicant, manager, supervisor or direct service staff, the Administrator confirms that Level 2 background screening has been completed and the person is eligible (see STF-02). No one works in these roles until eligibility is confirmed.
The governing body designates in writing a qualified backup for each Facility Operator. The backup's name and [PHONE] are posted in the office area and given to all staff.

The Facility Operator, or the backup in the operator's absence, is on site or reachable by phone at all times. The on-call schedule is posted a week ahead, and the on-call person must be able to respond to the home when needed.
The home keeps a designated office area for records, schedules and confidential files. The Facility Operator keeps it secured, and only authorized staff have access.

The Facility Operator reviews each home's staffing monthly against the number and characteristics of residents and the Residential Habilitation hour minimums (see STF-01 and GOV-05). Where residents' needs require more than the minimum, the Facility Operator adds staff and documents the reason.
The Facility Operator reports to the governing body at least quarterly on census, staffing, incidents, grievances, training status, inspections and outstanding corrective actions.
The governing body keeps current proof of the financial ability to operate the home, as required for licensure, and reviews it at least annually.

Each year the Administrator prepares the sworn statement of costs for APD-funded residents. The governing body or owner reviews the supporting figures and signs only after that review. A copy of the filed statement and its supporting figures is kept in the administrative file.
The governing body confirms annually that the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan has been reviewed and updated (see ENV-03).

The Facility Operator tells the Administrator and governing body immediately about any APD inspection finding, licensing notice, reportable incident or protective investigation involving the home (see GOV-07, BSP-04).
The governing body keeps minutes of its meetings, including decisions on staffing, budget, policy approval and corrective actions.
The Administrator keeps written job descriptions for the Facility Operator, backup and supervisors. Each person signs a copy acknowledging the duties.

The governing body evaluates the Facility Operator's performance at least annually against licensing compliance, resident outcomes, and quality-improvement results (see GOV-04) and documents the evaluation.

responsibilities.duty: Holds the license, ensures financial ability and adequate resources, appoints a qualified Facility Operator, reviews and approves the annual sworn cost statement, and oversees compliance.
Maintains the organizational chart, screening and qualification verification, annual cost statement preparation and records of governing body actions.
Runs the home day to day, is on site or on call at all times, ensures adequate staffing above the minimum when needed, and makes sure staff follow this manual.
Assumes the Facility Operator's responsibilities and decision authority during the operator's absence.

documentation: Organizational chart and governing body minutes
Facility Operator qualification file (transcripts or experience verification)
Screening eligibility records for owner, managers, supervisors and staff
On-call and backup schedules
Proof of financial ability
Annual sworn statement of costs with governing body review sign-off
Monthly staffing reviews and quarterly reports to the governing body
Facility Operator annual performance evaluation

policies.title: Licensure, Waiver Provider Enrollment and Provider Agreements
policies.applies_to: Owner/licensee, Administrator, Facility Operator/Program Director
policies.purpose: To make sure each home holds a current APD facility license and that [AGENCY NAME] is properly enrolled and authorized to provide Residential Habilitation under the iBudget Florida waiver.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not accept or serve an APD-funded resident in any home that is not licensed by APD, because APD cannot fund an unlicensed facility. Each home is licensed separately for a one-year term. [AGENCY NAME] will also complete waiver provider enrollment: the APD Provider Service Listing Letter, AHCA Medicaid provider enrollment, and the Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553). It will submit each license renewal at least 45 days before expiration and will keep local zoning authorities informed.

definitions.definition: The one-year license issued by an APD Regional Office for a specific group home or foster care facility under s. 393.067, F.S. and Chapter 65G-2, F.A.C.
The process of being approved to provide waiver services. It includes the APD listing letter, AHCA Medicaid enrollment, and the signed Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement.
The provider agreement on AHCA Form 5000-3553 that binds the provider to waiver and handbook requirements.
A home zoned and sited under s. 419.001, F.S. Homes of 6 or fewer residents are treated as single-family use; homes of 7 to 14 residents must be in multifamily zoning.

procedures: Before opening a home, the Administrator confirms the site meets zoning and siting requirements: no more than three APD facilities within 1,000 feet, single-family use for homes of 6 or fewer, and multifamily zoning with local government approval (60 days to approve or deny) for homes of 7 to 14.

The Administrator prepares the license application for each home separately, using Form 65G-2.002-A (no license fee is listed on the current form), and attaches all required documents, Level 2 screening results, proof of financial ability, the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan, and the policies in this manual.
The Administrator schedules the annual fire inspection with the local fire authority early enough that an approved inspection is on file before initial licensure and again before each renewal.

The application is complete only when all documents, screenings and a satisfactory APD inspection are in place. The Facility Operator corrects every deficiency cited before the license can issue. The Administrator tracks deficiencies in a corrective action log with due dates.
The Administrator records the license effective and expiration dates for each home in a licensure calendar and sets reminders at 120, 90 and 60 days before expiration.

The Administrator submits each renewal at least 45 days before expiration. A late or incomplete renewal is treated as an initial application, so the Administrator reviews the packet against the checklist before submission and keeps proof of submission.
The current license for each home is posted or kept readily available as APD directs.
After the first resident is placed, the Administrator notifies the local zoning authority in writing and files a copy.

For waiver enrollment, the Administrator applies through the APD Regional Provider Enrollment office for the Provider Service Listing Letter and, after listing, completes AHCA Medicaid provider enrollment through the Medicaid portal.
The Administrator signs and files the Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553). The governing body reviews it before signature and again whenever it is renewed or amended.

The Administrator confirms with APD the behavior focus or intensive behavioral designations that [AGENCY NAME] intends to offer. [AGENCY NAME] will serve residents under such designations only when the designation is approved and qualified monitoring and training are in place (see BSP-01).

The Administrator keeps current copies of the license, listing letter, Medicaid enrollment confirmation and agreement for each home, and notifies APD in writing of any change that affects them (see GOV-06).
Before closing a home, the Administrator gives APD 30 days' written notice (see GOV-06 and PCS-05).
The Administrator reviews licensure and enrollment status at each governing body meeting and reports any lapse risk immediately.
If a license is denied, suspended or revoked, or APD issues a violation notice, the Administrator notifies the governing body the same day and follows GOV-07.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares and submits applications and renewals, tracks deadlines, maintains enrollment records and communicates with APD, AHCA and zoning authorities.
Corrects deficiencies, ensures the home is ready for inspection and keeps the license available.
Reviews and authorizes applications and the provider agreement, and ensures resources for compliance.

documentation: License applications (Form 65G-2.002-A) and proof of submission
Current license for each home
Licensure calendar and renewal tracking log
Approved fire inspection reports
Zoning approvals and first-resident notification
APD Provider Service Listing Letter
AHCA Medicaid enrollment confirmation
Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553)
Deficiency and corrective action log

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Facility Operator/Program Director, governing body and all staff who use this manual
policies.purpose: To make sure this Policy & Procedure Manual is complete, current, approved, and available to staff and regulators, and that required policies are reviewed on schedule.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains written policies for each topic that Chapter 65G-2, F.A.C. requires, including admission and termination criteria, resident funds, behavioral responses, sexual activity, and video monitoring criteria if video is used. Policies are submitted with the license application and the waiver provider application. All policies are reviewed at least annually, and sooner when a rule, handbook or agency practice changes. The Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan is reviewed at least annually, and emergency and reactive-strategy procedures receive an annual internal review under Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C.

definitions.definition: A policy that carries an ID, version number, effective date and approval signature and is issued from a master copy.
A record of changes to Chapter 65G-2, the iBudget handbook, and rate rules, with the date reviewed and policy actions taken.
The yearly written evaluation of emergency and reactive-strategy procedures required by Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C. for providers that use them.

procedures: The Administrator keeps one master copy of the manual, with each policy showing its ID, title, version, effective date, last review date and approver.
The governing body approves each new or revised policy in writing before it takes effect. The approval date is recorded on the policy and in meeting minutes.

The Administrator confirms that the manual contains written policies for admission and termination criteria, resident funds, behavioral responses, sexual activity, and video monitoring criteria (if video monitoring is used), and checks that each matches the rule requirements.
The Administrator includes the manual with the APD license application and the waiver provider application and keeps a copy of the version submitted.
The Administrator reviews every policy at least annually and records the review date and any changes. Policies not reviewed within 12 months are flagged to the governing body.
The Administrator reviews the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan at least annually with the Facility Operator and updates it as needed (see ENV-03).

If [AGENCY NAME] uses reactive strategies, the Facility Operator completes an annual internal review of emergency procedures, uses incident and restraint data, and keeps the written review in the quality file (see BSP-02, GOV-04).

Chapter 65G-2 rules were largely amended on March 26, 2026. The Administrator keeps a rule-change log and checks the Florida Administrative Register and APD announcements monthly for new rules, handbook updates and rate tables.
Within 30 days of a rule change affecting practice, the Administrator drafts policy revisions and submits them to the governing body for approval.
Because the text of Chapter 65G-8 is under revision by APD, the Administrator confirms the current text before each annual review.
When a policy changes, the Administrator trains affected staff before the effective date. Staff sign a training acknowledgment that is placed in their personnel file.

A current copy of the manual is kept in the designated office area and is available to all staff at each home. Superseded versions are marked and kept for 6 years, and obsolete copies are removed from the home.
New staff read and sign acknowledgment of the manual sections relevant to their role during orientation (see STF-04).
The Administrator provides policies to APD or other regulators on request during inspections and monitoring (see GOV-07).
Findings from incidents, grievances, inspections or quality reviews that expose a policy gap trigger a policy review within 30 days.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the master manual, version control, annual reviews, rule-change log and staff training on changes.
Approves policies and revisions and reviews the annual review status.
Keeps the current manual at the home, ensures staff follow it and reports gaps to the Administrator.
Read and follow current policies and sign acknowledgments.

documentation: Master manual with version history
Governing body approval minutes
Annual policy review records
Rule-change log
Staff acknowledgment and training sign-in sheets
Annual CEMP review record
Annual internal review of emergency/reactive-strategy procedures
Copy of policies submitted with applications

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, Facility Operator/Program Director, nurse/health oversight staff and supervisors
federal: 42 CFR 441.302(a)(6) (HCBS assurances: monitoring of health and welfare)
policies.purpose: To monitor the health, safety and quality of services through regular data review, to prevent recurrence of incidents and errors, and to review every death for contributing factors.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a quality improvement program that reviews all APD incident reports and follow-up actions, including preventive measures to avoid recurrence; medication-error data; reactive-strategy data; and the annual evaluation of emergency procedures. Staff are retrained when there is evidence of medication errors. Every unexpected death is a critical incident reported within 4 hours, and every death is reviewed for contributing factors, with the review recorded in the quality improvement file. This work supports the state's assurance that the health and welfare of waiver participants are monitored.

definitions.definition: A serious incident, including an unexpected death, that requires initial notice to APD within 4 hours and a completed Incident Reporting Form (OP 3-0006) within 1 calendar day.
A structured internal review of the circumstances, health history, care provided and possible contributing factors of a resident's death, aimed at preventing future harm.
The confidential file in which trend reports, reviews, corrective actions and follow-up results are kept.

procedures: The Facility Operator forwards every incident report (APD Form OP 3-0006) to the Administrator within 1 calendar day of its completion, along with the follow-up report due within 5 days where required.

Each month, the Administrator and Facility Operator review all incident reports for the month. They record the type, time, location, people involved, root cause and preventive measures taken to avoid recurrence.
Each month, the nurse or health oversight person reviews all medication errors and near misses. The review identifies staff, shift, medication and cause.

When the review shows evidence of medication errors, the Facility Operator retrains the staff involved, and the retraining is documented before that staff member administers medication again (see HLT-01).

Each quarter, the Administrator compiles data on incidents, medication errors, injuries, behavioral events, grievances, elopements, hospital visits, missed medical appointments and staff turnover, and reports the trends to the governing body.

If [AGENCY NAME] uses reactive strategies, the Administrator reviews each use of a reactive strategy each month for appropriateness, documentation and notification, and refers patterns to the behavior analyst for plan review (see BSP-01, BSP-02).

Each year, the Administrator completes and records the annual evaluation of emergency and reactive-strategy procedures required by Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C. The evaluation covers data, staff certification status, and any needed changes.
For every trend or concern, the governing body assigns a corrective action with a responsible person and due date. The Administrator tracks it to completion and reports the result.

On the death of any resident, staff follow HLT-05. An unexpected death is a critical incident: staff notify APD within 4 hours and submit the completed OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day, and they call the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately if abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected.

Within 14 days of a death, the Administrator convenes a mortality review with the Facility Operator, nurse or health oversight person, and the person's support coordinator or other relevant professionals. The review covers diagnoses, recent changes in condition, medications, diet, supervision, equipment, emergency response and follow-up of medical appointments.
The mortality review is recorded in the QI file. It lists contributing factors, whether any policy or practice should change, and assigned actions. It is shared with the governing body.
The Administrator cooperates fully with any external review, investigation or mortality review requested by APD or other authorities and provides all records on request.
The Administrator checks that each corrective action has been carried out, and re-reviews the data in 90 days to see whether the action worked.
QI information is kept confidential and in line with RTS-04. Reports to the governing body use resident identifiers only when needed.
The Administrator updates policies and training when QI results show a need (see GOV-03, STF-04).

responsibilities.duty: Reviews QI data and mortality reviews quarterly and assigns and verifies corrective actions.
Leads the QI program, compiles data, schedules and records mortality reviews and tracks corrective actions.
Submits incident and error data on time, carries out corrective actions and retrains staff.
Reviews medication errors and health events and takes part in mortality reviews.

documentation: Monthly incident review summaries
Medication error and retraining records
Reactive-strategy use review (if applicable)
Annual emergency procedure evaluation
Quarterly QI trend reports and governing body minutes
Corrective action log
Mortality review records and critical incident notices
QI file

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation (iConnect)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, billing staff, Facility Operator/Program Director and direct support staff
policies.purpose: To make sure Residential Habilitation is billed accurately, only for authorized services actually delivered, with supporting documentation, and in compliance with Medicaid program integrity rules.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services covered by a Waiver Support Coordinator-issued authorization, at the rate set by the individual's support level and county group in Rule 59G-13.081, F.A.C. It bills the monthly rate when the individual is in the home for 24 or more days in the month and the daily rate otherwise, never bills days of absence, and staffs each home to at least the handbook minimum direct-care hours per resident per 24 hours. APD room-and-board claims are filed within 90 days after month end. Knowingly submitting a false claim violates federal and state law.

definitions.definition: The approved service, amount, and dates for a person on the iBudget waiver, issued through the Waiver Support Coordinator.
The Residential Habilitation rate billed per month when the individual is in the home 24 or more days, or per day otherwise.
Hours of direct care per resident per 24 hours: Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11.
APD's web-based system for provider documentation and communication. Access requires completion of iConnect training.
The form used to claim APD room-and-board payment.

procedures: Before admission, the Administrator confirms that the individual has an active iBudget authorization for Residential Habilitation at the correct support level and that the Waiver Support Coordinator has issued it. No service is billed before the authorization is in place (see PCS-01).

Each month the Facility Operator confirms the individual's support level and county group and the rate in Rule 59G-13.081, F.A.C. The Administrator checks the rule for updates, including the pending July 2026 rate table, and applies a new rate only when it is effective.
Staff record daily attendance in the home on the resident's daily record, including overnight absences, hospitalizations, home visits and the reasons.

After month end, billing staff count the days the individual was in the home. They bill the monthly rate if the count is 24 or more and the daily rate for the actual days otherwise. They do not bill days the individual was absent.
Before each claim is submitted, the Facility Operator reviews and signs a verification confirming that the daily documentation, staffing schedules and attendance support the billed days.

The Facility Operator schedules staff so that each home meets or exceeds the handbook minimum direct-care hours for each resident's level. The Administrator checks the actual schedules monthly against the minimum and keeps the comparison (see STF-01).

Staff who will use APD iConnect complete the required iConnect training with a score of 75% or more before getting access (Handbook Appendix B). The Administrator keeps the certificates and disables access promptly when a staff member leaves.

Staff complete the implementation plan, daily notes, quarterly summary and annual report required by the handbook and file them as directed (see PCS-03). Billing staff confirm those documents are current before claims are submitted.

The Administrator confirms the current handbook before relying on any electronic visit verification requirement. EVV in iConnect applies to personal care and home health, not Residential Habilitation, and any change is added to the rule-change log (see GOV-03).

For behavior focus or intensive behavioral rates, the Administrator confirms the designation, qualified monitoring and staff training are in place and documented before billing that rate (see BSP-01).
The Administrator files the APD room-and-board claim on Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end and keeps proof of filing. Room and board charged to the individual follows RTS-05.
The Administrator investigates any billing error immediately. Overpayments are reported and refunded as required, and the cause is corrected.

Any staff member who suspects false billing or missing documentation reports it to the Administrator or the governing body without fear of retaliation. The governing body reviews and documents the response.

Billing records, authorizations, schedules and daily documentation are retained as required by the Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement and available to APD, AHCA and federal reviewers on request (see GOV-07, REC-01).
The governing body reviews billing compliance, including any denied or recouped claims, at least quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees billing, authorization checks, rate updates, iConnect access, room and board claims and corrections.
Count billable days, prepare claims from verified records and keep supporting files.
Verifies attendance and documentation, staffs to the minimum hours and signs the pre-billing verification.
Complete accurate, timely daily documentation.
Reviews compliance reports and makes sure staff may report concerns safely.

documentation: Authorizations from the Waiver Support Coordinator
Daily attendance records
Monthly pre-billing verification
Actual staff schedules compared to minimum hours
iConnect training certificates
Claims and remittance records
Form 65G-13.008A and proof of timely filing
Overpayment and correction records
Implementation plans, quarterly summaries and annual reports

policies.title: Change of Ownership, Census, Capacity and Closure Notices
policies.applies_to: Owner/licensee, Administrator, Facility Operator/Program Director
policies.purpose: To make sure APD is notified, in the time required, of changes in ownership, census, capacity, transfers and closure of a home.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] notifies APD before accepting each new resident and reports census changes in writing within 5 calendar days. It requests capacity changes 30 days ahead, with a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance. It serves only residents whose characteristics match the license. It gives APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home. It obtains APD approval before transferring a resident between its own facilities, except in an emergency. Change of ownership follows Rule 65G-2.0021, F.A.C.

definitions.definition: Any admission, discharge, transfer, death or other change in the residents living in the home.
The maximum number of residents APD authorizes in a specific home, together with the resident characteristics stated on the license.
A transfer of the license holder's ownership interest or control that is subject to Rule 65G-2.0021, F.A.C.
Ending operation of a licensed home.

procedures: The Facility Operator keeps a current census for each home showing each resident's name, admission date and characteristics, and compares it to the licensed capacity and characteristics on the license before each admission.

Before accepting a new resident, the Administrator confirms that the person's characteristics match the license, then notifies APD in writing before the person moves in (see PCS-01). The notice is kept in the resident's file and the administrative file.
If a person's characteristics do not match the license, [AGENCY NAME] does not admit the person and the Administrator documents the reason.

The Facility Operator reports every census change to APD in writing within 5 calendar days after it occurs, including admissions, discharges, transfers and deaths. A copy of each report and proof of delivery is kept.

To request a capacity change, the Administrator submits a written request to the APD Regional Office at least 30 days before the proposed change. The request includes a passed fire inspection and evidence of zoning compliance. No additional resident is accepted until APD approves.

Before moving a resident between facilities that [AGENCY NAME] operates, the Administrator obtains APD approval in advance, except in an emergency. In an emergency, the Facility Operator notifies APD as soon as possible and documents the emergency (see PCS-05).

For a change of ownership, the governing body consults Rule 65G-2.0021, F.A.C. and the APD Regional Office before any agreement is signed, and the Administrator reviews the full rule text to build the checklist for the transaction.

The Administrator submits the notice and application required for the change of ownership within the time the rule sets and makes sure that screening, financial proof and other license documents for the new owner are complete.

The Administrator informs the Waiver Support Coordinators, AHCA enrollment and zoning authority of any change of ownership, and updates the Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement as required (see GOV-02).
Residents, guardians and advocates are told in writing of any ownership change affecting their home, and assurance of continuity of care is documented.
Before closing a home, the governing body approves the decision in writing. The Administrator then gives APD at least 30 days' written notice.

During the closure notice period, the Administrator works with each resident, guardian and Waiver Support Coordinator on a transition plan to a new setting, following PCS-05, and keeps a record of choices offered and decisions made.
The Administrator arranges for the transfer of residents' records, funds and property according to REC-01 and RTS-05 and completes the final property inventory.
On closure, the Administrator returns or surrenders the license as APD directs and keeps required records for the retention period.
The Administrator reviews census and capacity compliance monthly and reports any discrepancy to the governing body immediately.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares and files all notices, requests and applications and tracks deadlines.
Keeps accurate census, confirms resident characteristics match the license and reports changes within 5 calendar days.
Approves ownership change, capacity change and closure decisions.

documentation: Current census log for each home
Pre-admission notices to APD
Census change reports with proof of delivery
Capacity change requests, fire inspection and zoning evidence
Inter-facility transfer approvals
Change of ownership filings
30-day closure notice and transition plans
Governing body minutes

policies.title: APD Monitoring, Inspections and Corrective Action
policies.applies_to: Administrator/Facility Operator, Program Director, designated Monitoring Custodian, and all direct support staff on duty during an APD visit
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is always ready for, and cooperates fully with, monitoring and inspection by the Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD). It also sets how violations are tracked, corrected and prevented from recurring.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will admit APD Regional Office staff who show state identification at any time residents are in the home. It will produce the records APD requests within the required time frames. APD monitors licensed homes at least monthly, including at least one weekend visit each year, and reviews the home on site within 30 days after the first admission (Rule 65G-2.0032, F.A.C.). Resident records are open to APD staff for inspection and duplication, and a complete copy will be provided as soon as possible and no later than 2 calendar days after the request (Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C.). Personnel records, schedules and training documentation will be provided to APD within 3 calendar days of request. APD staff may observe fire drills. The Administrator designates a Monitoring Custodian who is responsible for producing documents on monitoring days. Every violation or deficiency will be logged, corrected by a stated date, and reviewed for root cause. The agency understands that violations are classified, fined and may lead to denial, suspension or revocation of the license under Rules 65G-2.004, 65G-2.0041 and 65G-2.005, F.A.C. (effective 3/26/2026).

definitions.definition: A scheduled or unannounced APD on-site review of the home, residents, staff, records and environment. APD conducts these at least monthly, including one weekend visit a year.
The staff member designated by the Administrator to maintain the monitoring-day document set and produce records to APD, with a named backup.
A documented step that fixes a cited deficiency or violation. It includes the responsible person, the completion date and the proof of correction.
The APD on-site review of the home within 30 days after the first admission.
Every day of the week, including weekends and holidays, when counting record-production deadlines.

procedures: The Administrator designates in writing a Monitoring Custodian and a backup, and posts their names and [PHONE] numbers in the staff office and on the shift handoff sheet.

The Monitoring Custodian keeps a Monitoring Readiness Binder (paper or secure electronic) in a central location. It contains: current license, most recent fire inspection, fire drill log, CEMP, census and capacity documents, house rules, Bill of Rights, staffing schedules, and the corrective action log.

Before the first admission, the Administrator confirms the home is ready for APD's on-site review, which APD will conduct within 30 days after the first admission, and keeps the admission documents for each resident ready for review.
All staff are trained at orientation and annually that APD staff with state identification may enter the home when residents are present. Staff must never delay or refuse entry.

When an APD representative arrives, the staff member on duty asks to see state identification, records the name, agency, time of arrival and purpose in the visitor log, and immediately calls the Monitoring Custodian or Administrator.
If the Custodian or Administrator is not on site, the staff member on duty cooperates, lets APD proceed, and does not leave the residents unsupervised.
The Custodian accompanies the APD representative, answers questions factually, and does not alter, backdate or create records during the visit.

For resident record requests, the Custodian provides immediate access for inspection and duplication. A complete copy of the record is delivered as soon as possible and always within 2 calendar days of the request. The date and time of the request and of delivery are documented.

For requests for personnel records, schedules or training documentation, the Custodian assembles the complete files and delivers them to APD within 3 calendar days of the request. The Custodian documents the date of request and delivery and keeps a copy of what was sent.

If APD requests proof of the agency's ability to operate for 60 days without state payment, the Administrator and the agency's financial representative prepare and submit the proof by the date APD sets, and keep a copy in the monitoring file.
When APD staff request to observe a fire drill, staff cooperate fully. The drill is conducted according to ENV-02, with no drills between midnight and 5:00 a.m.
At the end of each visit, the Custodian requests an exit discussion, writes down every finding or concern raised, and asks APD to state any deadline for correction.

Within 1 business day of the visit, the Custodian enters each finding in the Corrective Action Log with the finding, rule cited, responsible person, correction due date, and date and proof of completion.
The Administrator reviews the log, assigns each item, and approves any written response or plan of correction. The response is submitted to APD by the date APD requires.
Corrections that affect residents' health or safety are made immediately. The Administrator notes the date and time the hazard was corrected and the interim safeguards used.
The Administrator verifies each correction in person, signs the log, and keeps the proof (photographs, receipts, training sign-in sheets, revised forms).
Each month, the Administrator reviews the log for repeat or related findings, conducts a root cause review, and reports trends to the Quality Improvement review under GOV-04.

The Administrator reviews every notice of violation, fine or proposed license action against Rules 65G-2.004, 65G-2.0041 and 65G-2.005, F.A.C., and responds in writing within the time stated in the notice.
The Custodian updates the binder after each visit and at least quarterly, and conducts an internal mock monitoring review at least every six months.

responsibilities.duty: Designates the Custodian and backup, approves responses to APD, ensures corrective actions are completed and verified, and responds to violation or license-action notices.
Maintains the readiness binder, accompanies APD staff, produces records on time, and maintains the Corrective Action Log.
Ensures staff know the monitoring procedure, supports corrections, and conducts mock reviews.
Verify identification, admit APD staff, notify the Custodian, continue resident supervision, and never alter records.

documentation: Visitor log entries for every APD visit
Monitoring Readiness Binder contents and update dates
Record request and delivery log (resident records within 2 calendar days; personnel/training records within 3 calendar days)
Corrective Action Log with proof of completion
Written responses and plans of correction sent to APD
Mock monitoring review reports and QI minutes

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: All residents, legal representatives, and all staff
policies.purpose: To protect the rights of every person living in the home under the Florida Bill of Rights for persons with developmental disabilities and to meet the federal home and community-based services (HCBS) settings requirements for provider-owned or controlled residential settings.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] honors every right in s. 393.13, F.S., including dignity, privacy and humane care; freedom from abuse, neglect, exploitation and unnecessary restraint, isolation or excessive medication; religious freedom; social interaction and community participation; exercise and recreation; and the right to vote (Rule 65G-2.009(1)(b), F.A.C.). Placement in the home does not terminate or restrict the rights of parents or guardians (Rule 65G-2.009(1)(c)). Consistent with 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4), each resident has a lease or equivalent residency agreement, a lockable bedroom door, choice of roommate, access to food and visitors, freedom to decorate, and control over their own schedule. Any modification of these rights is allowed only through RTS-02. Chores appropriate to age and ability are encouraged but never required (Rule 65G-2.009(1)(a)7). No resident is discriminated against in this publicly funded program.

definitions.definition: The rights of persons with developmental disabilities listed in s. 393.13(3), F.S.
The federal requirements at 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) for residential settings owned or controlled by a provider.
A lease or other written agreement giving the resident the same responsibilities and protections from eviction as tenants under Florida landlord-tenant law, or an equivalent agreement.
A guardian under ch. 744, F.S., or guardian advocate under s. 393.12, F.S., acting within the scope of the court order.
Any limit on an HCBS right that is supported by a documented person-centered justification under RTS-02.

procedures: At or before admission, the Program Director gives each resident and legal representative a copy of the Bill of Rights (the APD published version) in a format and language they understand, and reviews it with them using plain language or the communication method in RTS-07.
The Program Director documents the review of rights on the Rights Acknowledgment form, signed by the resident or representative and by the staff member, and files it in the resident record.
The Administrator posts the Bill of Rights and the Florida Abuse Hotline number (1-800-962-2873) in a common area where residents can see them, at a height and in a format that residents can read.

Before move-in, the Administrator executes a lease or equivalent residency agreement with each resident or representative that states the services, the room and board amount, and the resident's protections. A copy goes to the resident and a copy is kept in the record.

Each bedroom door has a working lock that the resident controls. The Administrator keeps a master key in a secured location. Staff use it only in an emergency or with the resident's permission, and every use is documented on the Key Access Log.
The support team asks each resident about roommate preference before any room assignment and again at each annual planning meeting, and documents the preference and outcome.

Residents may access food and beverages at any time. Staff do not lock the kitchen or pantry, or limit meals or snacks, except through an approved modification under RTS-02 and any diet order under ENV-05.
Residents may have visitors at the times they choose, subject only to the resident's own preferences. Staff must not require visitor approval from staff or set blanket visiting hours.
Residents choose how to decorate and furnish their bedrooms. The Program Director supports them with safe options and records choices in the support plan.
Staff support each resident's own daily schedule, including bedtime, waking, meals, community outings and religious observance, and note choices and refusals in the daily notes.
Staff help each resident who wishes to vote to register, get information and get to the polls or request a ballot, and document that assistance.
The Program Director explains chores in the house rules as encouraged, age-appropriate and ability-appropriate, and never requires them or uses them as a condition of other services or privileges.

Staff never state or imply that a parent's or guardian's rights ended on admission. Representatives are invited to planning meetings and are told of significant changes in a resident's life in line with RTS-06.
Staff knock and wait for permission before entering any bedroom or bathroom, except in an emergency.

If a staff member believes a right has been violated, they report it immediately to the Program Director. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported to the Florida Abuse Hotline under BSP-03.
The Administrator reviews each resident's rights status at least annually and at each support plan review. Any needed modification is processed under RTS-02.

The Program Director monitors compliance monthly using a Rights and Settings checklist covering doors and locks, food access, visitors, privacy and decorating, and records results for QI review under GOV-04.
All staff are trained on this policy at orientation and annually, and the training is documented under STF-04.

responsibilities.duty: Executes residency agreements, controls master keys, posts rights notices and ensures settings comply with HCBS requirements.
Reviews rights with residents and representatives, runs the monthly checklist and addresses concerns.
Honor rights in daily practice, support choices, and report suspected violations immediately.
Is informed of rights and may raise a concern at any time through RTS-03.

Lease or residency agreement

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Program Director, behavior analyst, support coordinator liaison, and all direct support staff
policies.purpose: To make sure no right of a resident is restricted without a documented justification, informed consent, required review and the opportunity to challenge it.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not restrict any right except as permitted by law and only with due process. Under s. 393.13, F.S., no behavioral program may be implemented unless it has been reviewed under APD rule, which for behavior analysis services means the Local Review Committee (LRC) process in Chapter 65G-4, F.A.C. Restraint and seclusion are limited to the strategies permitted by Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C., and are never used for punishment or staff convenience. Any restriction of an HCBS right requires a documented person-centered justification, less intrusive alternatives that were tried, informed consent, and periodic review in the person-centered plan, as required by 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F). Residents and legal representatives will be told that they may challenge any restriction.

definitions.definition: Any limit on a resident's rights under s. 393.13, F.S., or the HCBS settings requirements, such as limiting access to food, visitors, money, belongings or the community.
The committee that reviews and approves or disapproves written behavior plans containing restricted procedures under Chapter 65G-4, F.A.C.
An emergency procedure used in response to dangerous behavior and governed by Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C.
A written statement of the specific assessed need for a restriction, the less intrusive methods tried, and how the restriction is proportionate.
Voluntary written agreement by the resident or legal representative after being told of the reason, risks, duration and right to refuse or challenge.

procedures: No staff member may impose a restriction on a resident on their own initiative. Staff who believe a restriction may be needed notify the Program Director the same day.

The Program Director convenes the support team (resident, legal representative, Waiver Support Coordinator, behavior analyst if involved, nurse as needed) to determine whether a restriction is justified.
The team documents the specific assessed need, the behavior or risk, and the positive interventions and less intrusive alternatives already tried and why they were not enough.

The team writes a person-centered justification that describes the proposed restriction, sets a time limit and a date for periodic review, identifies how data will be collected to measure its effect, and states that the restriction will cause no harm to the resident.

The Program Director gives the resident and legal representative a clear explanation, using the communication methods in RTS-07, of what is proposed, why, how long, and that they may refuse or challenge it. Written informed consent is obtained before the restriction begins.

Where the restriction is part of a behavioral program, the plan must be written or supervised by a certified behavior analyst and reviewed under APD rule. The Program Director sends the written plan to the LRC chair within 5 working days after implementation.

If the LRC disapproves a plan, the behavior analyst revises it and resubmits within 14 working days. Staff follow only the version approved by the LRC and the legal representative, and any disapproved element is stopped.

Staff may use restraint or seclusion only in the circumstances and by the methods allowed under Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C., only by staff who hold current certification in an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum, and never as punishment or for staff convenience. Details are in BSP-02.
Procedures listed as prohibited under Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C., are never used. Any use of a reactive strategy is documented and notified as required by BSP-02 and BSP-04.

The Program Director adds each approved restriction to the resident's person-centered support plan through the Waiver Support Coordinator (PCS-02) and files the consent, justification and LRC approval in the resident record.
Staff implement the restriction exactly as written and record the daily data required. They report any problems, injuries or the resident's objection to the Program Director.

The team reviews each restriction at the date set in the plan, at least annually, and whenever a team member requests. The restriction ends as soon as the need no longer exists. Continued restrictions need a renewed justification and consent.

The Program Director provides the resident and legal representative with the names and contact information of the Waiver Support Coordinator, the APD Regional Office [PHONE] and the Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873, and explains how to file a grievance under RTS-03 or request a review.
Remote video monitoring is never used in bedrooms or bathrooms. Any other use must follow RTS-09.
The Administrator reviews all active restrictions quarterly to confirm that each has current consent, justification and review. Results go to the QI review under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no unauthorized restrictions exist and reviews all active restrictions quarterly.
Convenes the team, obtains consent, submits plans to the LRC on time and ensures records are complete.
Writes or supervises behavior plans, revises disapproved plans within 14 working days and trains staff.
Follow approved plans only, collect data and report concerns.
Includes approved restrictions in the person-centered plan and takes part in reviews.

documentation: Person-centered justification for each restriction
Signed informed consent

Restriction review notes and dates

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All residents, legal representatives, families, support coordinators and staff
policies.purpose: To give residents and others a clear, safe way to raise concerns and have them resolved, while ensuring that allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation always go to the Florida Abuse Hotline and not through internal review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] welcomes concerns and complaints from residents, guardians, families, Waiver Support Coordinators and others, and no one will be retaliated against for raising one. Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation are reported immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 (ss. 39.201 and 415.1034, F.S., as incorporated by Rule 65G-2.010(6)(a), F.A.C.) and are never handled only through this internal process. The Hotline number and the APD Regional Office contact are posted in the home and at each phone extension (Rule 65G-2.010(1), F.A.C.). Residents and their representatives may also go directly to the Waiver Support Coordinator or the APD Regional Office. Notice of Medicaid fair hearing rights is provided whenever services are denied, reduced, suspended or terminated. Resident government and house-rule consultation is one avenue for resident concerns under Rule 65G-2.009(1)(d)-(e), F.A.C.

definitions.definition: A complaint or concern about services, staff, house rules, the home or a resident's rights that is not an allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation.
The Florida Department of Children and Families Abuse Hotline, 1-800-962-2873, which takes reports of abuse, neglect and exploitation 24 hours a day.
The hearing process available when Medicaid services are denied, reduced, suspended or terminated, under 42 CFR 431 Subpart E.
Any adverse action, threat or change in treatment because a person raised a concern or participated in a complaint.

procedures: At admission, and annually, the Program Director explains the grievance process to the resident and representative in plain language and in the method of communication they use (RTS-07), and records the review in the resident record.

The Administrator posts, in a common area and at every phone extension, the Florida Abuse Hotline number 1-800-962-2873, the APD Regional Office contact [PHONE], and the Administrator's contact [PHONE]. The posting is checked monthly.

Any staff member who receives a complaint, whether spoken, written or shown by behavior, accepts it respectfully, helps the person put it in writing if they wish, and gives it to the Program Director by the end of the shift.

If a complaint contains any allegation or suspicion of abuse, neglect or exploitation, the staff member reports it immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873, then notifies the Administrator and follows BSP-03 and BSP-04. It is not delayed for internal review.

The Program Director logs the grievance on the Grievance Log with date, complainant, description and any immediate action taken, and gives the complainant a written or other accessible acknowledgment within 2 business days.
The Program Director investigates by reviewing records and speaking with those involved, and makes sure that no staff member who is the subject of the complaint investigates it.
The Program Director gives the complainant a written resolution, explained in an accessible way, within 14 calendar days of receipt, or an update explaining the delay and a new date.
If the complainant is not satisfied, the Administrator reviews the matter personally, meets with the complainant if requested and issues a final written response.

At every step, the complainant is told they may also contact the Waiver Support Coordinator, the APD Regional Office or the Florida Abuse Hotline, and that they may have a support person or advocate with them.

If the grievance involves a denial, reduction, suspension or termination of services, the Administrator provides the written notice of Medicaid fair hearing rights and the process to request a hearing, and coordinates with the Waiver Support Coordinator.
Staff must never discourage, punish or retaliate against anyone for making a complaint. Any suspected retaliation is reported to the Administrator immediately and addressed under STF-07.
Residents may raise concerns through resident government meetings and house-rule consultation. The Program Director records concerns raised and the response at the next meeting.
The Administrator reviews the Grievance Log quarterly for trends, makes changes where patterns show a problem, and reports findings to QI under GOV-04.
Grievance records are kept confidential under RTS-04 and retained in line with REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures postings are current, conducts final reviews and prevents retaliation.
Logs, investigates and resolves grievances within the stated time frames and educates residents.
Accept complaints, report abuse, neglect or exploitation to the Hotline immediately, and pass other complaints to the Program Director.
Available to residents and representatives as an independent avenue for concerns.

documentation: Grievance Log
Written acknowledgments and resolutions
Fair hearing notices
Monthly posting check
Resident government meeting notes
Quarterly trend review

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, contractors and anyone with access to resident information
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy of residents and the confidentiality of their records, while allowing required access by APD and other authorized parties.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] treats all resident and client records as confidential under s. 393.13, F.S. (Rule 65G-2.009(5)(e), F.A.C.). Records are kept on the premises, or electronically in a central location, and cash and current financial information are secured (Rule 65G-2.009(4)(h)). A copy of records is retained for 6 years in accordance with HIPAA (Rule 65G-2.009(5)(g)). Records are open to APD and State of Florida agents who show identification (Rule 65G-2.009(5)(f)). Staff respect resident privacy and self-determination to the maximum extent possible, including when supervising (Rule 65G-2.009(6)(a)), and knock before entering bedrooms. Written consent is required before a resident's image, name or information is used for fundraising (Rule 65G-2.009(10)). The agency follows HIPAA (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164) and, if any resident receives substance use disorder treatment records covered by 42 CFR Part 2, those rules as well.

definitions.definition: Any information that identifies a resident or relates to their health, services, finances, behavior, family or history.
Individually identifiable health information covered by HIPAA, in any form.
Sharing only the information needed for the purpose of the disclosure.
A signed written permission from the resident or legal representative to share specific information with a specific party for a specific purpose and period.

procedures: At hire, each staff member signs a confidentiality agreement and receives training on this policy. Training is repeated annually and recorded under STF-04.
The Administrator designates a Privacy Officer, named on the staff contact list, to answer privacy questions and handle privacy complaints.
