The facility operator reviews the home for design suited to residents' disabilities, such as ramps, grab bars, wide doorways, roll-in showers and non-slip floors. Needed modifications are listed in the resident's plan and scheduled by [ADMINISTRATOR NAME].
Each bedroom is furnished with a bed, dresser, shelf space, window coverings and linens. Residents choose their own furnishings, bedding and decorations and may decorate their rooms.

Under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4), the home provides a lease or equivalent residency agreement, bedroom doors that lock (with only appropriate staff holding keys), choice of roommates, access to food at any time and visitors at any time. Any modification is justified and documented under RTS-02.

Maintenance staff measure hot water at resident-accessible outlets at least monthly. Water temperature must not exceed 120°F. Readings are logged, and any reading above the limit is corrected immediately.
Smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are installed, tested monthly and the batteries replaced as needed. Test results are recorded.
Portable heaters are not used in bedrooms of homes of 6 or fewer residents. Heating and cooling equipment is maintained.
Pools and other water hazards are fenced, locked or otherwise restricted. Supervision requirements for residents who swim are in each resident's plan.
Cleaning supplies, chemicals, and other hazardous items are locked or otherwise secured out of reach of residents who may be harmed by them. Safety data sheets are kept in the home.
The home has a designated office area with secure, locked storage for resident records and personnel records, accessible only to authorized staff under RTS-04 and REC-01.
The facility operator performs a documented walk-through of the home at least monthly using a checklist covering all items above, and records repairs, who is responsible and the date completed.
Once a year, before renewal, the facility operator reviews the home against the current full text of Rules 65G-2.007 and 65G-2.0072 and updates the checklist to reflect any rule change.
Before any renovation, capacity change or change in use of a room, the facility operator notifies the APD Regional Office and receives approval where required, under GOV-06.
Residents' requests for repairs or changes to their rooms are recorded and answered within a reasonable time, with the outcome shared with the resident.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the home complies with standards; handles zoning, APD notices and records; schedules repairs and inspections.
Performs and logs water temperature checks, detector tests and repairs.
Report hazards immediately, keep hazards secured, and support residents in decorating and caring for their rooms.
Choose how their personal space is furnished and decorated and report problems.
Provides funds for repairs and for modifications needed for accessibility.

documentation: Bedroom and living space measurement record
Siting and zoning verification and first-resident zoning notice
Monthly environmental checklist and repair log
Hot water temperature log
Smoke and carbon monoxide detector test log
Accessibility assessment and modification records
Lease or residency agreements and any HCBS modification justification
Annual rule-comparison review record

policies.title: Fire Safety, Fire Inspection and Monthly Fire Drills
policies.applies_to: The facility operator/program director, all DSPs and other staff, and all residents of the group home
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from fire by requiring an annual fire inspection, monthly fire drills, posted emergency numbers and a working telephone, as set out in Rule 65G-2.010, F.A.C.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] obtains an approved fire inspection each year under Ch. 69A-38, F.A.C., before initial licensure and before each renewal. The agency conducts a fire drill every month, never between midnight and 5:00 a.m., and keeps drill records for one year. Emergency numbers are posted at every telephone extension, and at least one telephone is accessible to staff and residents at all times.

definitions.definition: A practice evacuation of the home carried out as if there were a real fire, using the posted exit routes.
An inspection by the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal under Ch. 69A-38, F.A.C., that finds the home acceptable.
Any telephone, including each handset or line, in the home.

procedures: The facility operator requests the annual fire inspection from the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal at least 60 days before the license expires, and before the initial license application is submitted.
The approved fire inspection report is filed in the facility file and a copy is provided to the APD Regional Office with the license application or renewal.

If the inspection finds deficiencies, the facility operator corrects them promptly, records the correction date and requests re-inspection. The license application or renewal is not submitted without an approved inspection.
The facility operator schedules a fire drill every calendar month. Drills are not conducted between midnight and 5:00 a.m.
Drills are rotated across shifts and weekdays, and the exits used are varied so that every staff member and resident practices more than one route.
The staff member conducting the drill records the date, time of day, exit points used, evacuation time and signs the record.
During each drill, staff check that all residents leave the home, use planned assistance for those with mobility, sensory or cognitive needs, and meet at the designated safe place outside.
Staff review each drill's results with residents afterwards and fix any problems. Residents who did not understand are re-taught, and the facility operator is told about problems within one day.
Fire drill records are kept for one year, and original records are kept in the home for APD review.
APD Regional Office staff are allowed to observe monthly fire drills. The facility operator schedules drills so that staff are present who can run the drill when APD visits.

Emergency numbers are posted at every phone extension. They include law enforcement, the fire department, each resident's doctors, ambulance, the support coordinator, the Regional Office, the APD emergency on-call number, the Florida Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873) and Poison Control.
The facility operator verifies posted numbers monthly and updates them whenever a resident's doctor or other contact changes, or a resident moves in or out.
At least one working telephone is accessible to staff and residents at all times. If a landline or cell service fails, staff use a charged backup phone and tell the facility operator.

Exit routes are posted in each bedroom and common area, kept clear of obstructions, and checked at each shift change. Fire extinguishers, alarms and detectors are checked and serviced according to the fire authority's requirements and the facility checklist.
New staff are shown the exit routes, fire extinguisher locations and drill procedure on their first shift and before working alone, under STF-04.
Any fire, smoke event or activated alarm that results in injury, displacement or damage is reported under BSP-04 and REC-02.

responsibilities.duty: Requests and tracks inspections, ensures monthly drills are done and recorded, and maintains posted numbers.
Conduct drills as assigned, assist residents to evacuate and record results.
Checks and services detectors, extinguishers and alarms and keeps exits clear.
Take part in drills to the extent of their ability and tell staff about concerns.

documentation: Approved annual fire inspection report
Fire drill record: date, time, exits used, evacuation time and signature (retained for one year)
Drill rotation schedule and notes on follow-up
Posted emergency number list and monthly verification
Maintenance records for detectors, alarms and extinguishers
Staff orientation record covering exit routes and drills

policies.title: Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP), Evacuation and Emergency Shelter
policies.applies_to: The facility operator/program director, all staff and all residents of the group home
policies.purpose: To make sure residents are protected during hurricanes, fires, floods and other emergencies by having a written, current, staff-trained Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan and by meeting APD reporting rules for evacuation and emergency sheltering.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written CEMP as required by s. 393.067, F.S., and Rule 65G-2.010, F.A.C. The CEMP is updated as needed and at least annually, and all staff are trained within 30 days of hire and annually. If the home is evacuated by order, [AGENCY NAME] reports to the APD Regional Office within 6 hours and every 6 hours after, and does not reoccupy until cleared. If the home shelters people above licensed capacity during a declared emergency, [AGENCY NAME] reports to APD within 48 hours and keeps a log of everyone sheltered.

definitions.definition: The home's written Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan, prepared on the APD template.
An evacuation directed by a government authority, including a mandatory evacuation order.
Sheltering people in the home beyond the licensed capacity during a declared emergency, where it is safe.

procedures: The facility operator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) prepares the CEMP on the APD template and keeps it in the home where all staff can find it, with a copy in the office. A copy is provided to the APD Regional Office as requested.
The CEMP addresses hazards, including hurricane, tornado, flooding, fire, hazardous materials and power outage in extreme weather.
The CEMP describes care of residents who stay in the home, including food, water, supplies, medication, staffing and communication.
The CEMP describes care of residents who are evacuated: transfer of records, transportation, shelter location, supplies, staffing and medications.
The CEMP identifies residents with mobility limits or other needs and the support and equipment each requires to evacuate or shelter in place.
The CEMP describes coordination with local emergency management and post-disaster activities, such as responding to family inquiries and reporting to county emergency management.
The CEMP assigns specific staff to each part of the plan, with backups, and lists contact numbers for staff, families, guardians, the support coordinator, the nurse and the APD Regional Office.
The facility operator reviews and updates the CEMP at least annually and whenever the home, residents, shelter location or contacts change. Each update is dated and signed.
All staff are trained on the CEMP within 30 days of hire and annually, after the annual update. Training is recorded in each personnel file under STF-04.

Each resident has a go-kit with medication supply and administration records, identification, a recent photo, current care and behavior information, equipment, comfort items and contact numbers. The kit is checked at least monthly and before storm season.

When a storm or other hazard is forecast, the facility operator decides whether to shelter in place or evacuate, checks supplies, fuel, vehicles and generator needs, and notifies guardians, families and support coordinators.
If the home is evacuated by order, the facility operator reports to the APD Regional Office within 6 hours of the order and every 6 hours after until the evacuation is complete.
The facility operator names a contact person who can be reached 24 hours a day by APD until residents return. The contact name and phone number are given to the Regional Office.
Residents return to the home only after the facility operator confirms authorities have cleared it and the home is safe. Utilities, food, medications and equipment are checked before return.

If the home shelters people above licensed capacity during a declared emergency and conditions are safe, the facility operator keeps a log showing each person's name, usual address and arrival and departure dates. The facility operator reports to APD within 48 hours.
After any activation, the facility operator holds a debrief with staff, notes lessons learned and updates the CEMP. Injuries, deaths or missing residents are reported under BSP-04, BSP-05 and HLT-05.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares, updates and trains on the CEMP; makes evacuation and sheltering decisions; makes required reports to APD.
Advises on medication, equipment and medical needs in the plan and during activation.
Complete training, carry out assigned duties, keep residents safe and calm and keep go-kits stocked.
Take part in planning to the extent of ability; give contact and medical information.

documentation: Current CEMP with annual review date and signature
Staff CEMP training records (within 30 days of hire and annually)
Resident go-kit checklists
Evacuation notices to the APD Regional Office with times and 6-hour updates
Sheltering log (names, usual address, arrival and departure dates) and 48-hour report
Post-event debrief notes and plan revisions

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers and contractors working in the group home, and residents
policies.purpose: To reduce the spread of infection among residents and staff through consistent hygiene, cleaning, safe handling of blood and body fluids, staff training and exposure response.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] sets its own infection prevention practices through this policy and OSHA requirements. Rule 65G-2.017, F.A.C. (Health Safety Standards) was repealed effective March 26, 2026, and is no longer the source of these practices. All staff complete an HIV/AIDS educational course within 90 days of providing direct services. Hazardous chemicals are secured, potentially toxic first aid kit materials are stored safely, and vehicles are kept clean and in proper working order. The Department of Health does not inspect APD-licensed homes, so the facility operator is responsible for monitoring compliance.

definitions.definition: Basic infection control practices applied to every person, including hand hygiene, gloves and other protective equipment and safe handling of body fluids.
Contact of eyes, mouth, mucous membranes or non-intact skin with blood or other potentially infectious material, or a needlestick or sharps injury.
Gloves, gowns, masks, eye protection and similar items worn to prevent contact with infectious material.

procedures: Staff use standard precautions with all residents at all times, regardless of known diagnosis.

Staff wash hands with soap and water, or use alcohol-based hand rub when hands are not visibly soiled, before and after resident care, meal preparation, medication administration, using the toilet, glove use and contact with body fluids.
The home keeps a stocked supply of disposable gloves, soap, hand sanitizer, tissues, trash liners and appropriate PPE in accessible locations. The facility operator checks supplies weekly.

Staff wear gloves for any contact with blood, body fluids, wounds, soiled linens or incontinence care, and discard them after each task. Gowns, masks or eye protection are used when splashing is likely.
Sharps, such as lancets and needles used for health care, are disposed of in puncture-resistant containers that are kept out of reach of residents and replaced when full.
Blood and body fluid spills are cleaned immediately using PPE and an appropriate disinfectant according to its label. Contaminated waste is bagged and disposed of properly.
Soiled laundry is handled with gloves, kept separate from clean laundry and washed at the temperature and with the detergent appropriate for the item.
Bathrooms, kitchens and high-touch surfaces are cleaned and disinfected on a set schedule posted in the home. Cleaning is documented.
Staff observe food safety practices described in ENV-05, including hand washing, separating raw and cooked foods, proper storage and temperatures.
Residents are supported with their own personal hygiene items. Razors, toothbrushes, towels and similar items are not shared.

Staff report signs of illness in residents, such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea, rash or cough, to the nurse or health care provider under HLT-04. When directed by a health care provider, the resident is supported in staying separated from others, and staff follow isolation or precaution instructions.
Staff with symptoms or a diagnosed communicable disease follow STF-05 and do not work with residents when their condition poses a risk, until cleared.
All staff complete an HIV/AIDS educational course within 90 days of providing direct services, and the certificate is filed in the personnel record under STF-04.

Training on bloodborne pathogens, hazard communication and the use of this policy is provided at orientation and at least annually. The facility operator offers the hepatitis B vaccine to staff with occupational exposure risk, as OSHA requires, and records acceptances or declinations.

After an exposure incident, the staff member washes the area immediately, reports to the facility operator and receives prompt medical evaluation. The incident is documented and reported as required under BSP-04, and confidentiality of the source and the staff member is protected.

Cleaning products and chemicals are stored in locked or secured areas out of residents' reach where required. Safety data sheets are kept in the home and staff are shown how to read them under 29 CFR 1910.1200. Potentially toxic first aid kit materials are stored safely.
Vehicles used to transport residents are cleaned regularly and kept in proper working order, with spill kits and disinfectant wipes carried in the vehicle.

When the health department or a health care provider requests information about an outbreak or a reportable condition, the facility operator cooperates and shares only the information that law allows under RTS-04.
The facility operator reviews infection-related events, such as illnesses or exposures, at least quarterly under GOV-04 and corrects any problems.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains this policy, supplies and training; monitors compliance; handles exposure follow-up and records.
Advises on infection control, isolation and resident health concerns.
Use standard precautions, clean and disinfect as assigned, report illness and exposures.
Take part in hygiene routines with support as needed.

documentation: HIV/AIDS course certificates and bloodborne pathogen training records
Hepatitis B vaccine acceptance or declination forms
Cleaning schedules and logs
Supply inventory checks
Exposure incident reports and medical follow-up records
Illness reports and notices to health care providers
Safety data sheet binder

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
policies.applies_to: All DSPs and other staff who shop for, prepare, serve or assist with food, the nurse and health care coordinator, and all residents
federal: 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(i) (access to food at any time)
policies.purpose: To make sure residents receive safe, nutritious meals that meet their health needs and preferences, that prescribed diets are followed exactly, and that residents keep access to food and the kitchen as people living in their own home.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides meals as required by Rule 65G-2.007, F.A.C., and carries out all diets and directions ordered by a medical or health care professional. Staff are trained on diet changes after medical appointments. Special instructions for assisting with meals are recorded in the resident record. Residents may take part in meal planning, shopping and preparation, which is encouraged but never required, and have access to food and the kitchen consistent with HCBS settings rules.

definitions.definition: A diet ordered by a physician or other health care professional, such as a texture-modified, low-sodium, diabetic, allergy-safe or thickened-liquid diet.
Written instructions for how to assist a resident to eat or drink safely, including positioning, pacing, utensils and supervision level.
Any restriction on a resident's access to food, which is a rights restriction that requires justification and documentation.

procedures: At admission and at least annually, the nurse or health care coordinator and DSPs record each resident's diet orders, allergies, food preferences, cultural and religious food practices and swallowing or choking risks in the resident record.

Meals and snacks are planned with each resident and follow the meal provisions in Rule 65G-2.007. Menus are based on residents' preferences and nutritional needs, posted where residents can see them, and substitutions are available.

Residents may choose to join in planning menus, grocery shopping and preparing meals. Participation is offered and encouraged but never required, and residents' choices are documented in the support plan.
Diet orders and instructions from medical or health care professionals are written in the resident record and posted discreetly in the kitchen so that every staff member can see them.

After each medical, dental, dietitian or speech-language appointment, the DSP or nurse reviews any new or changed diet instructions with the facility operator and updates the resident record that day.
The facility operator or nurse trains all staff who work with the resident on any change in diet before the next meal. The training is recorded, with the staff member's signature.

Special instructions for assisting a resident with meals, including positioning, utensils, pacing and level of supervision, are recorded in the resident record and followed at every meal. Staff do not leave residents at risk of choking unattended while eating. Further choking precautions are under HLT-03.

Food is stored, prepared and served safely: refrigerated foods are kept cold, hot foods are kept hot, raw and ready-to-eat foods are kept separate, and expired or spoiled food is discarded. Staff wash hands and follow ENV-04.
Residents with allergies have their allergens listed and posted, and staff check labels before serving. Cross-contact with allergens is prevented in preparation and storage.

Residents have access to food, drinks and the kitchen at any time, consistent with the HCBS settings rule. They may keep personal snacks where their safety allows, and food is not used as a reward or punishment.

If a resident's health or safety requires limiting access to food or the kitchen, such as for a resident with Prader-Willi syndrome or severe pica, the limit is a documented rights restriction. It has a specific assessed need, less intrusive methods tried first, consent, periodic review and a plan to end it, under RTS-02. Staff do not impose such limits on their own.

Staff monitor residents' eating, drinking and weight as ordered and report changes such as refusing meals, weight loss or gain, dehydration, coughing during meals or difficulty swallowing to the nurse or health care provider under HLT-04.
The home maintains a supply of food for residents' preferences and for emergencies as required by the CEMP under ENV-03.
Poison Control and each resident's doctors' phone numbers are posted at every phone extension under ENV-02, for use in cases of food poisoning, allergic reaction or choking.
The facility operator reviews meal practices, menus and diet compliance during monthly walk-throughs and asks residents about their satisfaction. Concerns are handled under RTS-03.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures meals meet the rule, diet orders are carried out and staff are trained; reviews compliance monthly.
Records diet orders and swallowing risks; advises on diet changes; trains staff.
Prepare and serve meals safely; follow diets and mealtime instructions; support resident choice; report changes.
Express preferences, take part in meal planning and shopping as they choose, and report concerns.

documentation: Diet orders, allergy lists and special mealtime instructions in the resident record
Posted menus and substitutions
Staff training records for diet changes
Appointment follow-up notes showing diet changes
Weight and intake records where ordered
Rights restriction documentation for any limit on food access
Monthly walk-through checklist

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff who drive or ride with residents, all vehicles used to transport residents (agency-owned, staff-owned or contracted), and the Facility Operator/Program Director.
policies.purpose: To make sure every trip is safe, every resident is accounted for at departure and arrival, no resident is ever left in a vehicle, and vehicles and drivers meet the standards in Rule 65G-2.009(14) and Rule 65G-2.008(4)(b), F.A.C.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] transports residents only in vehicles that meet the requirements below, driven by approved drivers who meet the driver standards of Rule 65G-2.008(4)(b). Staff keep a transportation record for every trip, initial it before each departure, and complete a vehicle sweep on arrival. Seating capacity, seatbelts and the staff-to-resident ratio are never exceeded or waived. Residents are transported at no cost unless a trip exceeds 25 miles. APD is notified before any resident is taken out of Florida. A resident left in a vehicle is a critical incident.

definitions.definition: The written log of each trip listing each resident transported, date and time of departure and arrival, and the driver's name and signature.
A physical inspection and visual check of the entire vehicle by the driver on arrival to confirm no resident remains inside.
A staff member authorized in writing by the Facility Operator/Program Director who holds a valid driver license and meets the driver standards of this policy.
A direct support professional who meets the qualification requirements of Rule 65G-2.008(2) without relying on the 90-day supervised alternative.
An incident requiring initial notice to APD within 4 hours under BSP-04, including a resident left in a vehicle.

procedures: Before a staff member drives residents, the Facility Operator/Program Director confirms and documents that the person holds a valid driver license and has had a driving history check showing no violation in the past 3 years relating to alcohol or drugs, and no moving violation that caused license suspension or revocation.
The Facility Operator/Program Director obtains an updated driving history for every approved driver at least once each year and removes the driving duty of anyone who no longer meets the standard.

Drivers obey all traffic laws and must not drive while impaired by alcohol, medication or any other substance. A driver who is impaired or unwell reports this to the supervisor and does not drive (see STF-05).
A DSP who is working the 90-day supervised alternative under STF-03 may transport residents only with an experienced DSP, who must stay within 100 feet of the DSP and residents at all times.

Before the first trip of each day, the driver checks the vehicle and records that it has a current license plate, proof of the state-required minimum insurance, a working fire extinguisher with a current tag, working seatbelts for every seat in use, working heat and air conditioning, and no unsafe condition. For vehicles with a wheelchair lift or tie-downs, the driver confirms they work.

The driver takes the vehicle out of service and reports to the Facility Operator/Program Director if any item in Step 5 fails. Residents are not transported in that vehicle until the problem is repaired and the repair is documented.

Before departure, the staff person in charge confirms that the number of residents does not exceed the manufacturer's seating capacity or the number of installed seatbelts. The person also confirms the staff-to-resident ratio required by each resident's plans (see STF-01) is met for the trip.

Before the vehicle leaves, each resident is seated and secured with a seatbelt or other appropriate restraint, and wheelchairs are secured with tie-downs. Adaptive equipment is used as described in HLT-07 and each resident's support plan.

Before each departure, staff list every resident on the transportation record and initial it to confirm each resident is accounted for. The driver signs the record with the date and time of departure.
During transport, the driver keeps the cabin temperature between 65 and 78 degrees Fahrenheit. No one smokes or vapes in any vehicle used to transport residents.

On arrival, the driver marks each resident off the transportation record, records the arrival time, and walks through the entire vehicle, including all rows and the cargo area, to confirm no resident remains. The driver signs the record after the sweep.

If a resident is found or discovered to have been left in a vehicle, staff immediately get the resident out, provide first aid or call 911 as needed (see HLT-04 and HLT-06), and notify the Facility Operator/Program Director. The Facility Operator/Program Director gives initial notice to APD within 4 hours and completes the incident report as required by BSP-04.

If transportation is provided by a contractor, [AGENCY NAME] assigns [AGENCY NAME] direct care staff to ride on the trip and perform the roster, departure initialing, arrival mark-off and vehicle sweep duties in Steps 9 and 11.

Residents are transported at no cost. If a single trip exceeds 25 miles, only the miles over 25 may be charged, and the charge is explained to the resident or representative in advance and recorded in the resident's funds record (see RTS-05).
The Facility Operator/Program Director notifies APD before any resident is taken out of the State of Florida and keeps a copy of the notice in the resident's record.

The Facility Operator/Program Director keeps maintenance, repair and inspection records for each vehicle and reviews the transportation records at least monthly for missing initials, signatures or sweep entries, and corrects any problem with the staff involved.

In a collision, breakdown or medical emergency during a trip, the driver stops safely, calls 911 if anyone may be injured, keeps residents safe, contacts the Facility Operator/Program Director, and completes an incident report under BSP-04.

responsibilities.duty: Approves drivers, obtains annual driving histories, ensures vehicles meet standards, reviews transportation records monthly, makes required notices to APD and keeps maintenance records.
Completes the vehicle check, observes capacity, seatbelt and ratio limits, signs the transportation record at departure and arrival, and performs the vehicle sweep.

responsibilities.role: Staff person in charge of the outing
responsibilities.duty: Initials the roster before each departure and confirms that each resident is secured and accounted for.
Accompanies any DSP in the 90-day supervised alternative on trips and stays within 100 feet.
Report vehicle defects, unsafe driving and any missing resident immediately.

documentation: Transportation records for each trip (resident names, date and time of departure and arrival, driver name and signature, departure initials, arrival mark-offs), kept at least 12 months
Driver approval, driver license copy and annual driving history in the personnel file
Vehicle registration, tag, insurance, fire extinguisher tag and daily vehicle check records
Vehicle maintenance and repair records, kept at least 12 months
Notice to APD for out-of-state travel
Incident reports for any resident left in a vehicle, collision or emergency
Record of mileage charges, if any

policies.title: Staffing Levels, Resident Supervision and Overnight Coverage
policies.applies_to: Facility Operator/Program Director, scheduling staff and all direct support staff of the [AGENCY NAME] group home.
federal: FLSA 29 CFR 552, 785 (home care and sleep time rules, as applicable)
policies.purpose: To make sure enough qualified staff are present at all times to meet each resident's needs, to meet the minimum direct-care hours required for Residential Habilitation, and to keep the schedules the rules require.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs adequate staff for the number and characteristics of its residents, even above any minimum. At least one staff person is present at all times while residents are in the facility, except under a Regional Office-approved written plan. Overnight coverage is set by each resident's needs under the support plan, behavior plan and Safety Plan. [AGENCY NAME] also meets the minimum direct-care hours per resident per day in the iBudget Waiver Services Coverage and Limitations Handbook. Volunteers and residents are never counted toward required staffing.

definitions.definition: Hours worked by qualified direct support staff providing care and supervision to residents. They are measured against the per-resident, per-day minimums in the handbook.
The Residential Habilitation level assigned to the resident (Basic, Minimal, Moderate, Extensive 1 or Extensive 2). It sets the minimum direct-care hours.
The staffing pattern described in the most recent license application approved by APD.
A written plan approved by the APD Regional Office before it is implemented, allowing a specific resident to be alone for limited periods.

procedures: The Facility Operator/Program Director keeps a current list of each resident's support level, behavior plan, support plan, Safety Plan, medically ordered care, court orders and other needs, and uses it to build every schedule.

The Facility Operator/Program Director sets the staffing pattern using APD's factors: resident level of need, behavior plans, support plans, Safety Plans, medically ordered care, court orders, number of residents, staff competency and range of services. The pattern must at least match the one approved in the most recent license application.

The Facility Operator/Program Director calculates the required daily direct-care hours by adding the handbook minimum for each resident (Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11). For example, six Moderate residents require at least 36 hours per day. The total may be met each day or averaged over a 7-day period, and the calculation is kept on file.

The Facility Operator/Program Director recalculates required hours whenever a resident is admitted, discharged, or has a change in support level, behavior plan or medical needs, and adjusts the schedule before the change takes effect.

At least one staff person is physically present in the home at all times that any resident is in the facility. No shift is left uncovered, and staff never leave until relieved by a qualified staff person.

A resident may be left alone only if a written plan for that resident has been approved by the APD Regional Office before it is used. The plan is kept in the resident's record and staff follow its limits exactly.

Overnight coverage is decided by the Facility Operator/Program Director and documented for each resident based on his or her needs, support plan, behavior plan and Safety Plan, and is reviewed whenever those documents change. The schedule shows who covers overnight, and the covering staff person is never left without a way to call for help.

When a new resident with a history of sexually aggressive behavior is placed, staff keep the resident under visual supervision whenever he or she is awake during the first 24 hours, and the schedule is built to make this possible.
Staffing is never met by volunteers or residents. Volunteers and residents may not be counted toward direct-care hours or ratios.
The Facility Operator/Program Director posts a written weekly schedule at least one week in advance in a place staff can see it. It shows each staff member by name and shift.
The Facility Operator/Program Director records the actual hours worked, including changes, trades and call-outs, and keeps the actual schedules for 6 months.

If a staff member calls out, the Facility Operator/Program Director or designated on-call person arranges a qualified replacement right away, and the departing staff member stays until relief arrives. If no replacement can be found, the Facility Operator/Program Director notifies [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and takes action to prevent any gap in supervision.

When residents leave the home on outings or transportation, staff keep the staff-to-resident ratio required for the trip and ensure that the staff left at home are still enough to supervise the residents who remain (see ENV-06).
Only staff who have cleared screening, completed required training and meet DSP qualifications are counted toward staffing (see STF-02, STF-03 and STF-04).

The Facility Operator/Program Director reviews the actual schedule against required hours at least monthly, documents any shortfall and the corrective action, and reports staffing problems to the governing body (see GOV-04).
The Facility Operator/Program Director sends copies of schedules to APD within 3 calendar days of a request.

Staff time is paid in accordance with the federal and state wage and hour rules, including those for overnight or sleep time, and any such arrangement is written and approved by [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] before use.

responsibilities.duty: Sets the staffing pattern, calculates required hours, builds and posts schedules, approves any alone-time plan request to the Regional Office, and reviews actual coverage monthly.
Report to shifts as scheduled, stay until relieved, supervise residents as planned and notify the supervisor of any gap or call-out immediately.
Arranges replacement coverage and responds to staffing emergencies.
Ensures resources are available to maintain staffing, and reviews staffing reports.

documentation: Daily direct-care hour calculation and required hours by resident
Approved staffing pattern from the most recent license application
Weekly posted schedules and actual schedules (kept 6 months)
Regional Office-approved alone-time plans, if any
Overnight coverage determination for each resident
Monthly schedule review and corrective action notes
Copies of schedules sent to APD within 3 calendar days of request

policies.title: Background Screening and the Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
policies.applies_to: The licensee/applicant, Facility Operator/Program Director, managers, supervisors, all direct support staff, and anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property.
policies.purpose: To make sure that every person who works in the home or has access to residents, their living areas, funds or property has passed Level 2 background screening, and that eligibility is tracked in the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires Level 2 screening under Chapter 435, F.S. and s. 393.0655, F.S., for the applicant, managers, supervisors, every direct service provider and anyone with access to residents' living areas, funds or property. Screening is submitted and tracked through the AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse. A person who is not eligible does not provide direct care or have access to any resident, funds or living setting. Exemptions from disqualification are granted only as provided in s. 435.07, F.S.

definitions.definition: Fingerprint-based state and national criminal history screening under Chapter 435, F.S.
The AHCA Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse, which stores screening results and eligibility status and is used by employers to register and track their screened staff.
The electronic fingerprinting method performed by a Clearinghouse-authorized vendor.
Any person required to be screened under this policy.
An offense listed in s. 393.0655, F.S., that makes a person ineligible unless an exemption is granted.

procedures: The Facility Operator/Program Director registers [AGENCY NAME] in the Clearinghouse before any hiring and names a Clearinghouse account administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME].
Before the first day of work, each covered person is told in writing that screening is required, and signs an acknowledgement of the screening requirement.
Each covered person goes to a Clearinghouse-authorized Livescan vendor for fingerprinting and gives the vendor [AGENCY NAME]'s Clearinghouse information so the results are routed to [AGENCY NAME].
The Clearinghouse account administrator checks the Clearinghouse for the person's eligibility result and prints or saves the result for the personnel file.

No applicant begins work, or has access to residents, their living areas, funds or property, until the Clearinghouse shows the person is eligible and the Facility Operator/Program Director has documented that review.

If the result shows the person is not eligible, the person is not hired, or is removed from all resident contact immediately, and the Facility Operator/Program Director records the date and action taken. Staff and volunteers who do not meet eligibility do not provide direct care or have access to any resident, funds or living setting.

If the person says he or she will request an exemption, [AGENCY NAME] does not allow work until an exemption has been granted under s. 435.07, F.S., and the Facility Operator/Program Director places a copy of the exemption in the personnel file.

The account administrator keeps each employee on [AGENCY NAME]'s Clearinghouse roster. When an employee leaves, the account administrator removes the person from the roster. The administrator reviews the roster and eligibility status at least monthly and takes action on any status change.

Staff must report any arrest or new charge to the Facility Operator/Program Director within one working day. If the arrest is for a disqualifying offense under s. 393.0655, F.S., [AGENCY NAME] treats it as a critical incident and gives initial notice to APD within 4 hours as required by BSP-04. The staff member is removed from resident contact pending eligibility review.

The Facility Operator/Program Director takes action to dismiss any worker who is determined ineligible. The licensee is responsible for each direct service provider's compliance, and refusal to dismiss a non-compliant worker can result in license denial or revocation.

Volunteers, interns, maintenance workers, contractors and any other person who has access to residents' living areas, funds or property are screened the same way as direct support staff, unless they are never left alone with residents and have no access to funds or property. Such a decision is made in advance in writing by [ADMINISTRATOR NAME].

At least once each year, the Facility Operator/Program Director checks the FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator database for registrants living within one mile of the home, and tells staff about any found. The check and staff notification are documented.
The Facility Operator/Program Director keeps screening results and Clearinghouse eligibility records confidential in the personnel file or in a separate secure file (see STF-06 and RTS-04).

If the Clearinghouse or Livescan vendor has a technical issue, the Facility Operator/Program Director contacts the AHCA Background Screening Unit at 850-412-4503 or bgscreen@ahca.myflorida.com and documents the contact. No one begins work until eligibility is confirmed.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures all required persons are screened, confirms eligibility before work begins and removes ineligible persons from resident contact.
Manages the Clearinghouse account, roster and status checks and keeps screening results.
Completes fingerprinting, reports arrests promptly and cooperates with screening.
Ensures the screening requirement is met and that ineligible workers are dismissed.

documentation: Signed acknowledgement of screening requirement
Livescan receipt and Clearinghouse eligibility result for each covered person
Dated record of eligibility review before the start of work
Exemption documents under s. 435.07, F.S., if any
Monthly Clearinghouse roster review
Annual FDLE Sexual Offender/Predator database check and staff notification record
Incident report for any arrest for a disqualifying offense

policies.title: DSP Qualifications, Hiring and Performance Evaluation
policies.applies_to: Facility Operator/Program Director, hiring managers and all applicants and employed direct support professionals (DSPs).
policies.purpose: To make sure that every DSP hired meets the minimum qualifications in Rule 65G-2.008, F.A.C., and the Residential Habilitation provider requirements, and that each DSP's performance is evaluated on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires only DSPs who are at least 18, pass Level 2 screening, hold a high school diploma or equivalent and have either the required experience or related education. A DSP without the required experience may work only under the 90-day supervised alternative with timely written notice to the APD Regional Office and a performance evaluation within 120 days. DSPs must be mentally competent, physically capable of their duties and unimpaired on duty. Wages are at or above the Florida minimum wage.

definitions.definition: An employee who provides direct care and supervision to residents of the home.
One year of experience in a medical, psychiatric, nursing or childcare setting, or working with persons with developmental disabilities.
30 semester hours, 45 quarter hours or 720 classroom hours in special education, mental health, counseling, guidance, social work, or health and rehabilitative services.
The option for a DSP without qualifying experience or education to work the first 90 days directly under the supervision of a qualified DSP under the same contiguous roof line.

procedures: The Facility Operator/Program Director writes a job description for the DSP position that lists duties, required qualifications and required skills, and gives a copy to each applicant.
Each applicant completes an application showing age, education and work history, and the Facility Operator/Program Director verifies that the applicant is at least 18 years old.

The Facility Operator/Program Director verifies a high school diploma or equivalent. Official transcripts, affidavits or other formal documents may establish equivalency, and a copy is kept in the personnel file.

The Facility Operator/Program Director verifies either one year of qualifying experience (by employer contact, reference or other documentation), or qualifying education of 30 semester hours, 45 quarter hours or 720 classroom hours, and places the proof in the personnel file.

The Facility Operator/Program Director confirms the applicant has cleared Level 2 screening under STF-02 before the first day of work, and completes Form I-9 employment eligibility verification as required by federal law.

The Facility Operator/Program Director assesses, with a documented interview, that the applicant is mentally competent and physically capable of the duties in the job description (including lifting, transferring and emergency response), and discusses the duty to be unimpaired while on duty (see STF-05).

If an applicant does not have the qualifying experience or education but is otherwise qualified, the Facility Operator/Program Director may hire the person under the 90-day supervised alternative. The Facility Operator/Program Director assigns a named qualified DSP to supervise the person directly under the same contiguous roof line for the first 90 days, and schedules them together.

Within 5 days after the start date, the Facility Operator/Program Director sends written notice to the APD Regional Office with the DSP's name and the facility name and keeps a copy of the notice and proof of delivery.
During the 90 days, the DSP takes residents out of the home only with an experienced DSP who stays within 100 feet. The DSP may transport only under the conditions in ENV-06.

The Facility Operator/Program Director performs and documents a written performance evaluation of the new DSP within 120 days of hire, reviewed with the DSP, who signs it. Evaluations continue at least annually, and more often if problems arise.
New DSPs complete orientation and required training on the schedule in STF-04. The Facility Operator/Program Director records the dates.
The Facility Operator/Program Director sets DSP pay at or above the Florida minimum wage, which is $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026, and reviews pay when the minimum wage changes.

The Facility Operator/Program Director ensures that Residential Habilitation provider qualifications, including any added requirements for behavior focus or intensive behavioral designations, are met for staff assigned to those residents (see BSP-01).
The Facility Operator/Program Director keeps the qualification proof, job description, evaluations and related records in the personnel file under STF-06.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies qualifications, makes hiring decisions, gives APD notice for the 90-day alternative, assigns the supervising DSP and completes evaluations.
Directly supervises the new DSP in the first 90 days and stays within 100 feet when outings occur.
Provides accurate qualification information, performs duties as written in the job description and takes part in evaluation.
Approves hiring practices and wage rates.

documentation: Job description and application
Proof of age, high school diploma or equivalent, and experience or education
Level 2 screening eligibility record and Form I-9
Written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days of hire for any 90-day alternative DSP and proof of delivery
Name of the supervising DSP and 90-day schedule
Performance evaluation within 120 days and annual evaluations
Wage records

policies.title: Direct Support Professional Orientation and Training
policies.applies_to: Facility Operator/Program Director and all direct support staff, including those assigned to residents with behavior plans, medication duties or access to resident funds.
policies.purpose: To make sure every DSP completes required training on time, is trained on each resident's individual plans before working with the resident, and that training records are kept and available to APD.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] trains all DSPs on the schedule required by Rule 65G-2.008(7), F.A.C., and related rules. Zero Tolerance training is completed before a DSP provides direct services. Staff do not administer medication until certified and validated, and do not use any reactive strategy until certified. Training records are kept for at least 3 years.

definitions.definition: Training on the detection, prevention and reporting of abuse, neglect and exploitation.
The APD-approved core curriculum for direct care staff.
The APD course under Chapter 65G-7, F.A.C. Unlicensed staff must pass it and be validated before administering medication.
An emergency intervention technique used in response to behavior, governed by Chapter 65G-8, F.A.C. and BSP-02.
The professional who trains staff on a resident's behavior plan.

procedures: The Facility Operator/Program Director keeps a training tracker for each DSP showing every required course, its date, the due date and the expiration date, and reviews it at least monthly.
Before a new DSP provides any direct services, the DSP completes Zero Tolerance training, and the training date is entered in the record. The training is repeated at least every 3 years.

On the first day, the DSP is oriented on [AGENCY NAME] policies, the Bill of Rights, house rules, emergency numbers, the reporting duties to the Abuse Hotline (1-800-962-2873) and the resident-specific information needed to work safely.
Within 90 days of first providing services, the DSP completes the APD Direct Care Core Competencies curriculum.
Within 90 days, the DSP completes classroom first aid, abdominal thrust and CPR training. Online-only training does not satisfy this requirement (see HLT-06).
Within 90 days, the DSP completes the HIV/AIDS course.
Within 30 days of hire, and again every year after the annual update of the emergency management plan, the DSP is trained on the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (see ENV-03).

A DSP who will administer medication takes the APD Basic Medication Administration course, scores at least 85% on the exam and 100% on the medication administration record (MAR) section, and is validated by an approved validator before administering any medication. The DSP completes an annual update and revalidates within the 60 days before the certification expires. Staff whose certification has lapsed do not give medication (see HLT-01).
Before working with a resident who has a behavior plan, each DSP is trained on the plan by a certified behavior analyst, and the trainer records the date and content.
For residents with a Safety Plan, each DSP completes Safety Plan training before working with the resident. All DSPs are trained on [AGENCY NAME]'s sexual activity policy (see BSP-07).
Staff with access to resident funds are trained on [AGENCY NAME]'s resident-funds procedures before handling funds (see RTS-05).

No staff member may use any emergency intervention or reactive strategy until the person has been certified in an APD-approved emergency procedure curriculum. Under Chapter 65G-8, the curriculum includes at least 12 direct training hours and a written test with an 80% minimum score. Certification is valid for one year, and staff are recertified before it lapses (see BSP-02). Before each annual review, the Facility Operator/Program Director confirms the current text of Chapter 65G-8 and the approved curriculum, because APD has revisions in development.

For staff who work with residents with a behavior focus or intensive behavioral designation, the Facility Operator/Program Director ensures completion of 20 contact hours of training and yearly recertification, as required by the iBudget handbook.
Staff who handle blood or body fluids receive bloodborne pathogens training annually (see ENV-04).

A DSP who has not completed a required course by its due date is not scheduled alone for the duties that depend on that course, and the Facility Operator/Program Director documents the corrective action.
The Facility Operator/Program Director keeps all training records, with certificates, sign-in sheets and test results, for at least 3 years and gives them to APD on request.

responsibilities.duty: Schedules and tracks all training, removes untrained staff from related duties, and keeps records.
Trains staff on each resident's behavior plan and documents attendance.
Conducts medication course training and validation as required.
Completes all training on time and keeps certificates current.
Ensures training resources are available and reviews compliance reports.

documentation: Individual training tracker with due dates
Certificates for Zero Tolerance, Direct Care Core Competencies, first aid/CPR, HIV/AIDS and medication administration
Medication validation and annual update records
Emergency management plan training sign-in sheets
Behavior plan and Safety Plan training records
Sexual activity policy and resident-funds procedures training records
Reactive strategy certification records
Bloodborne pathogens training record
Orientation checklist, signed by the DSP
Training records retained at least 3 years

policies.title: Employee Health, Fitness for Duty and Communicable Disease
policies.applies_to: All direct support staff and any employee working in the home.
federal: 29 CFR 1910.1030 (hepatitis B vaccination offer for exposed employees)
policies.purpose: To make sure staff are fit for duty, not impaired while working, and physically capable of performing their duties. It also sets how [AGENCY NAME] handles employee health information and communicable disease concerns in line with Rule 65G-2.008 and federal law.
policies.policy: No staff member may work while impaired by alcohol, medication or any other substance to the extent that normal faculties are affected. Staff must be physically capable of performing their duties. Rule 65G-2.008 does not require a TB test or physical exam for DSPs, and the former Health Safety Standards rule, 65G-2.017, was repealed effective 3/26/2026. Any pre-employment or ongoing health screening that [AGENCY NAME] requires is a facility policy choice, applied consistently to all staff in the same job class and handled with ADA-compliant medical privacy.

definitions.definition: Having the ability to see, hear, walk, talk, judge distances, drive, make judgments or act in an emergency affected by alcohol, medications or other substances.
Mentally competent, physically capable of performing the job duties with or without reasonable accommodation, and not impaired.
An illness that can be passed to residents or other staff, such as influenza, COVID-19, tuberculosis or gastrointestinal infection.
A file kept separate from the personnel file, with access limited to those who need it.

procedures: At hire, the Facility Operator/Program Director reviews the job description with each applicant, including the physical demands of the job, and asks whether the person can perform them with or without reasonable accommodation. Medical questions are asked only after a conditional offer and only as the ADA permits.

Staff must report to work unimpaired. Staff are told that working while impaired by alcohol, prescription or over-the-counter medication, or any other substance is prohibited and may lead to discipline up to termination.

Staff who take a medication that may affect alertness, driving or judgment tell their supervisor that they may be limited. The staff member does not have to name the medication or condition. The supervisor decides whether the staff member can work safely, drive residents or provide emergency response, and may adjust duties.

If a supervisor believes a staff member is impaired, the supervisor immediately removes the person from resident care and driving, arranges a safe ride home, and arranges for a qualified replacement so supervision is never interrupted (see STF-01). The supervisor documents the observed behavior in factual terms.

The Facility Operator/Program Director reviews the incident with the staff member within 2 working days, decides on follow-up under [AGENCY NAME]'s personnel policy and reports to [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] if there is any concern for resident safety or neglect (see BSP-03 and BSP-04).

Staff who become unable to perform physical duties because of injury or illness tell the supervisor. The Facility Operator/Program Director may ask for a health care provider's note limited to what the person can and cannot do, and considers reasonable accommodation.

Staff who have symptoms of a communicable disease, such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea, a new rash or persistent cough, do not work and call the supervisor before the shift. The supervisor arranges replacement coverage. The staff member returns when symptom-free or cleared by a health care provider, following the guidance in ENV-04.

[AGENCY NAME] adopts the following facility health screening practice, and the Facility Operator/Program Director applies it the same way to every DSP: after a conditional offer, each DSP completes a TB symptom and risk questionnaire, and any positive answer is referred to a health care provider before the person works with residents. This is a facility policy choice and not a rule requirement.

Staff who have a reasonably anticipated exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials are offered hepatitis B vaccination at no cost, as required by OSHA, and a signed acceptance or declination is kept (see ENV-04).

Health information, including notes, medication information and screening results, is kept in a confidential medical file, separate from the personnel file, and shared only with those who need to know (see STF-06 and RTS-04).

If a staff member's illness or condition may have exposed residents, the Facility Operator/Program Director notifies the nurse or health provider and acts under HLT-02 and ENV-04, and tells residents' representatives as needed.

A staff member who is found to be unfit for duty in a way that puts residents at risk is removed from resident care, and the Facility Operator/Program Director documents the removal, notifies [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] and reports to APD where reporting is required.

The Facility Operator/Program Director reviews this policy yearly and when rules change, and confirms the current text of Chapter 65G-2 so that employee health practices follow the rules in effect (see GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Applies fitness-for-duty standards, removes impaired staff, keeps confidential health records and arranges replacement coverage.
Observe staff at shift start, act on concerns about impairment and document factual observations.
Report to work fit for duty, report symptoms of communicable illness and limits on duties.
Reviews decisions that affect employment and ensures ADA compliance.

documentation: Job description with physical demands
Documentation of any fitness-for-duty concern and removal from duty
Confidential medical file entries, including health care provider notes and TB questionnaire results, if used
Hepatitis B vaccine acceptance/declination records
Absence and return-to-work records for communicable illness
Incident reports if resident safety was affected

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All full-time and part-time employees of [AGENCY NAME], including direct support professionals (DSPs), the Facility Operator/Program Director, relief staff and supervisors, at every licensed home.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] keeps complete, accurate, organized and retrievable personnel, training and scheduling records. These records show that staff are qualified, screened, trained and supervised, and that staff are paid and insured as the law requires. They must be ready for APD review and for production to APD within the required time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a separate personnel record for every full-time and part-time employee. It keeps a job description for every paid position, documentation of all facility staff training, and written staff schedules. Records are kept as Rule 65G-2.008(6) and (7), F.A.C. require, and copies are given to APD within 3 calendar days of a request. [AGENCY NAME] pays at least the Florida minimum wage, which is $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026, and carries workers' compensation coverage as required by s. 440.02, F.S. Coverage is mandatory for employers with four or more employees. Personnel records are confidential and are kept apart from resident records.

definitions.definition: A separate file for each full-time or part-time employee. It holds education, qualifications, experience, references, background screening, training participation and discipline, plus the payroll and employment-eligibility documents listed in this policy.
The record of who actually worked each shift, including substitutions, call-outs and overtime, as opposed to the planned weekly schedule.
A record of each training showing the date, content, trainer and attendees.
The 90-day supervised alternative to the experience or training requirement for a new DSP, which requires a 120-day performance evaluation in the file.

procedures: The Facility Operator/Program Director ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) creates a separate personnel file for each employee on or before the first day of work. Files are kept in a locked cabinet at [ADDRESS] or in a access-restricted electronic system.

The file contains the job application, the education record (high school diploma or equivalent), documentation of qualifying experience or related training hours, and at least [NUMBER] references with notes of any reference check.

The file contains background screening documentation (see STF-02), including the date of Level 2 screening results and the annual sexual offender/predator database check. A worker does not start work until the required screening result is in the file.

The file contains the signed job description, the offer letter or employment agreement, and the employee's acknowledgment of agency policies. A job description exists for every paid position and is reviewed whenever duties change.

The file contains the Form I-9 and its supporting documents, the W-4 and payroll tax set-up for FICA and income tax withholding. The Form I-9 is completed within the federal deadlines and is held in a section of the file separate from the performance and screening documents.

The file contains documentation of training participation (dates, content, trainer, attendees) as required by STF-04, including medication certification and validation under HLT-01, CPR/first aid, and Zero Tolerance training.
The file contains all discipline, counseling, investigation outcomes and any Corrective Action Plan, along with the employee's written response if offered.

For any DSP hired under the 90-day supervised alternative, the file contains the written notice sent to the APD Regional Office within 5 days of hire and the DSP performance evaluation completed within 120 days of hire. The Program Director calendars the 120-day date at the time of hire.
The Program Director keeps a facility-wide training log that records the date, content, trainer and attendees for every training. Training documentation is kept at least 3 years.

The Program Director writes the weekly work schedule and posts it in the home at least one week in advance. The schedule lists each shift and the staff assigned, so that coverage required by STF-01 is visible.

After each shift, the shift lead records any change from the posted schedule. The Program Director keeps the schedule of actual coverage for at least 6 months, and the weekly schedules are retained with it.

[AGENCY NAME] pays each employee at least the Florida minimum wage. Before September 30, 2026 the payroll administrator updates the pay scale so no employee is paid below $15.00 per hour from that date, and records the review in payroll files. Time and pay records are kept to meet FLSA 29 CFR 516 and 552.

The Program Director confirms before the first employee start date, and at each policy renewal, that workers' compensation coverage is active, and files the certificate of coverage in the administrative file. If the employee count reaches four or more, coverage is in force before the fourth person starts.

When APD requests personnel records, schedules or training documentation, the Program Director sends complete copies within 3 calendar days. The request date, the date sent, the method and the person who sent the copies are logged.

Each quarter, the Program Director audits a sample of personnel files against a checklist covering screening, qualifications, training, evaluations and schedules. Gaps are corrected within 14 days and the audit is reported under GOV-04.
Access to personnel files is limited to the Program Director, the owner/administrator, designated payroll staff, and APD or other authorized reviewers. An access log is kept for paper files.

When an employee leaves, the Program Director completes an exit checklist, retains the file as required by this policy and applicable payroll and employment record rules, and keeps training records at least 3 years.

responsibilities.duty: Creates and maintains complete personnel files, schedules and training records. Meets the 3-calendar-day production deadline. Audits files each quarter.
Keeps wage, tax and I-9 records. Confirms minimum wage compliance and workers' compensation coverage.
Records actual shift coverage and schedule changes at the end of each shift.
Provide accurate documents, report changes (address, license, driver history) promptly and sign training attendance records.

documentation: Personnel file for each employee (application, qualifications, references, screening, training, discipline, evaluation)
Job descriptions for each paid position
Facility training log (date, content, trainer, attendees), kept 3 years minimum
Weekly posted schedules and actual coverage schedules (kept 6 months minimum)
Notice to the Regional Office for DSPs hired under the supervised alternative and the 120-day evaluation
Form I-9, W-4 and payroll records
Workers' compensation certificate of coverage
APD record-request log showing the 3-calendar-day response
Quarterly personnel file audit

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, relief staff, volunteers, interns and contractors of [AGENCY NAME] who work in or have contact with residents of the home, and the licensee, owner and their family members.
policies.purpose: To protect residents' dignity, rights and finances by setting clear standards of professional conduct and boundaries. It also ensures staff report abuse, neglect and exploitation immediately, and that discipline is applied fairly and consistently.
policies.policy: Staff treat residents with dignity and respect and uphold the rights in s. 393.13, F.S. Staff do not use or benefit from residents' money or property, do not have sexual contact with residents, do not use forbidden responses to behavior, and do not use a resident's image for solicitation without written permission. Staff report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately to the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873. Violations lead to consistent discipline, and a verified finding triggers [AGENCY NAME]'s own discipline and, if the worker is retained, a Corrective Action Plan within 15 days.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a paid support relationship from a personal, financial, romantic or sexual relationship.
Improper use of a resident's funds, property or assets for the benefit of someone other than the resident.
Corporal punishment, noxious substances, verbal abuse, humiliation, and dark or locked time-out rooms.
A finding by the protective investigator that the allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation is verified.

procedures: At hire and annually, each staff member receives and signs this policy and the Code of Conduct. The signed copies are filed in the personnel record (see STF-06).
Staff address residents by their chosen names, respect privacy in bathing, dressing and personal care, and speak and act in ways that preserve dignity.

Staff do not borrow money or property from a resident, do not sell items to residents, do not accept gifts of more than nominal value and do not ask residents for favors. Any offered gift is reported to the Program Director.

Neither the licensee, employees nor their family members may be named beneficiary of a resident's life insurance (unless related to the resident by blood or marriage), receive indirect financial benefit from it, or borrow or use a resident's funds.
Employees may not gain any financial benefit by charging fees against or using resident funds. Personal funds are handled only as set out in RTS-05, with two-person counts and receipts.

Staff do not engage in sexual activity or sexual contact with any resident and do not sleep in resident beds. Staff follow the dress code and personal-space rules in the sexual activity policy (BSP-07).

Staff use only the interventions in the resident's approved behavior plan and BSP-01 and BSP-02. Corporal punishment, noxious substances, verbal abuse, humiliation, and dark or locked time-out rooms are never used.
Staff keep personal social media, texting and in-person relationships with residents professional. Staff do not post photos or information about residents on any platform.
Staff do not use a resident's image, story or information for fundraising, advertising or solicitation without written permission from the resident or authorized representative, under RTS-10.

Staff who know of or suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation call the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately, then notify the Program Director ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) at [PHONE] without delaying the hotline report. The Program Director completes incident reporting under BSP-03 and BSP-04. No staff member needs permission to report.
No staff member may retaliate against anyone who reports a concern or makes a good-faith report. Retaliation is a disciplinary offense.
Staff who are named in a protective investigation follow BSP-06, including removal from direct contact with the resident if needed to protect residents.

The Program Director investigates internal conduct concerns promptly, documents findings and applies discipline consistently for similar conduct, using progressive steps up to termination for serious violations.
If a verified finding is made against a worker who is retained, the Program Director completes a Corrective Action Plan within 15 days and files it in the personnel record and with APD as required.

Before hire and every month after, the Program Director checks every employee against the HHS-OIG exclusion list (42 CFR 455.2). The Program Director removes any excluded person from duty immediately, and records each check in the personnel file.
Staff who see a boundary concern in a coworker report it to the Program Director. Concerns are reviewed under GOV-04 for patterns and training needs.

responsibilities.duty: Follow this policy, protect resident funds and dignity, avoid forbidden responses and report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately.
Trains staff, investigates conduct concerns, applies consistent discipline, completes Corrective Action Plans within 15 days and runs exclusion checks.
Ensures the licensee and family members comply with the financial restrictions and supports enforcement of this policy.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy and the Code of Conduct
Abuse Hotline report confirmation numbers and incident reports
Conduct investigation notes and disciplinary records
Corrective Action Plan (within 15 days of a verified finding when the worker is retained)
Monthly HHS-OIG exclusion check log
Gift disclosure log
Written permissions for any use of a resident's image

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, update, store or release resident records, and all residents' records at every licensed home operated by [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident has a complete, current individual record on the premises that supports safe care and supervision, and that records and related documents are kept for the required time and produced to APD on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps an individual record for each resident on the premises (paper or electronic) that holds information pertinent to the resident's health, supervision and care. The record has all the contents required by Rule 65G-2.009(5), F.A.C. and is updated at least 30 days after new information is received. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a copy of each resident's record for 6 years, consistent with HIPAA. The original records are the resident's property and follow the resident on a move. A complete copy goes to APD no later than 2 calendar days after request.

definitions.definition: The file, paper or electronic, kept in the home for each resident with the contents listed in this policy.
A written list of the resident's personal belongings, updated every 12 months and 30 days before discharge.

The minimum time a record is kept: 6 years for individual records; 3 years for training; 1 year for fire drills, staff communication and funds receipts; 12 months for transportation and vehicle maintenance; 6 months for actual staff schedules.

procedures: At admission, the Program Director opens an individual record for each resident, kept in the home at [ADDRESS]. Electronic records are password protected and available to staff on duty during any shift.
The record includes the resident's name and date of birth, and the name, address and phone number of the physician and dentist.
The record includes contact information for the legal representative and the waiver support coordinator, and the resident's legal competency, guardianship status and authorized representatives.
The record includes written authorization for routine medical and dental care, signed by the resident or the authorized representative.
The record includes medical and dental reports and the medication history, with special instructions for carrying, lifting, positioning, bathing and meals.
The record includes the property inventory, a color photograph taken within the past five years, and every incident report involving the resident.
The record includes the current support plan and any implementation plan or behavior plan. The Program Director replaces outdated versions and moves them to the archive section of the file.

Staff update the record at least 30 days after new information is received (for example new diagnoses, medication changes, appointments, guardianship changes). The staff member who receives the information gives it to the Program Director, who files it and initials and dates the update.
The Program Director updates the property inventory every 12 months and again 30 days before any planned discharge. The resident or representative is invited to review and sign.
Staff keep the monthly personal funds accounting and all receipts of $25 or more for at least one year (see RTS-05).

The Program Director keeps fire drill records for 1 year, transportation records and vehicle maintenance records for 12 months, staff communication records for 1 year, staff training records for at least 3 years, and actual staff schedules for 6 months.

The Program Director retains a copy of each individual's record for 6 years, in line with HIPAA documentation retention (45 CFR 164.316). Closed records are kept in a locked, labeled location or secured electronic archive, and a destruction log is kept after the retention period ends.

When a resident moves, the Program Director gives the original record to the resident or the new provider, as the record is the resident's property, and keeps a copy for the retention period. The release is documented, with the date, items sent and the recipient.
When APD requests a record, the Program Director sends a complete copy no later than 2 calendar days after the request. The request date, send date and method are logged.
Records are released to others only as RTS-04 allows. Records are not left unattended and are not removed from the premises except for transfer, medical appointments or legal requirement.
Every quarter, the nurse or Program Director audits a sample of records for completeness and currency, and corrects gaps within 14 days. Results are reported under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains each record, keeps it current, controls access and retention, and produces copies to APD within 2 calendar days.
Give new information to the Program Director promptly, document accurately and protect confidentiality.
Ensures medical, medication and special-instruction content in the record is current.
Provides updated support plans and contact information for the record.

documentation: Individual record for each resident with all required contents
Record update log (30-day updates)
Property inventory (12-month and pre-discharge)
Personal funds accounting and receipts of $25 or more (1 year minimum)
Fire drill, transportation, vehicle maintenance, staff communication, training and schedule records (retention as stated above)
Record release/transfer log
APD record-request log (2-calendar-day response)
Record destruction log
Quarterly record audit

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: The Facility Operator/Program Director, the licensee/owner, nurse, shift leads and any staff who make or support reports to APD, the Florida Abuse Hotline, local zoning or Medicaid.
