policies.purpose: To give one place where [AGENCY NAME] lists every report, notice and filing it owes to the state, who is responsible and when it is due, so no deadline is missed and each report is documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] makes every required report to the Florida Abuse Hotline, the APD Regional Office, local zoning and Medicaid on time. Abuse, neglect and exploitation are reported immediately to the Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873. Critical incidents, reportable incidents, census, evacuation, capacity, staffing, licensing and closure reports follow the deadlines in this policy. Each report is documented with the date, time, method, recipient and person who made it. The Program Director keeps a master compliance calendar.

definitions.definition: A serious incident for which the Regional Office must be told within 4 hours, with the completed APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day.
An incident that must be reported to the Regional Office within 1 calendar day on Form OP 3-0006.
Any admission, discharge, transfer or death that changes who lives in the home.
The APD Regional Office that licenses and monitors the home.

procedures: The Program Director ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) keeps a master compliance calendar listing every report in this policy, its due date, and the staff member responsible, and reviews it weekly.

Abuse, neglect, exploitation: any staff member who knows or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation calls the Florida Abuse Hotline at 1-800-962-2873 immediately (see BSP-03). The staff member records the confirmation number and notifies the Program Director.
Critical incidents: the Program Director gives initial notice to the Regional Office within 4 hours and submits the completed APD Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 within 1 calendar day (see BSP-04).
Reportable incidents: the Program Director submits Form OP 3-0006 to the Regional Office within 1 calendar day.

Follow-up: the Program Director sends follow-up information within 5 days after reporting, and continues updates until the incident is resolved. Each update is dated and filed with the original report.
New admissions: before accepting a new resident, the Program Director gives notice to APD (see PCS-01), and confirms the resident's characteristics match the home's license under Rule 65G-2.006.
Census changes: the Program Director reports any census change in writing to the Regional Office within 5 calendar days.
Capacity changes: the Program Director requests any change in licensed capacity 30 days ahead, with a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance (see GOV-06).

Evacuation: when an evacuation is ordered, the Program Director or on-duty lead reports to the Regional Office within 6 hours and every 6 hours after, until residents return (see ENV-03). If an emergency shelter becomes over capacity, the report goes to the Regional Office within 48 hours.
Supervised-alternative DSPs: the Program Director sends written notice to the Regional Office within 5 days after a DSP starts under the 90-day supervised alternative (see STF-03).
Verified findings: when a verified finding is made against a worker the agency retains, the Program Director submits a Corrective Action Plan within 15 days (see BSP-06).
Records requested by APD: personnel records and schedules go within 3 calendar days (see STF-06), and individual resident records within 2 calendar days (see REC-01).

License renewal: the Program Director submits the renewal application at least 45 days before the license expires, with all documents, screenings and an approved fire inspection. A late or incomplete renewal is treated as an initial application.
Annual sworn cost statement: the licensee files the annual sworn statement of costs for APD-funded clients under s. 393.067(10), F.S., by the deadline APD sets.
Closure: the licensee gives APD 30 days' written notice before closing a home (see GOV-06).
Out-of-state travel: the Program Director notifies APD before taking any resident out of Florida.
Zoning: after the first resident is placed in a new home, the licensee notifies local zoning.

Data and enrollment: the Program Director and billing staff keep APD iConnect data and Medicaid enrollment information current, and update APD Provider Enrollment (see GOV-02 and GOV-05) when information changes.

Each report is logged with the date, time, method, recipient, and name of the person who made it. Copies are filed in the incident, administrative or resident record as appropriate. Late or missed reports are investigated and the cause corrected, and reported under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the compliance calendar, makes or delegates every report, and keeps the report log.
Files the license renewal, the annual sworn cost statement, closure notice and capacity requests, and keeps the licensing file current.
Report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to the Hotline immediately, and give incident information to the Program Director without delay.
Keeps iConnect and Medicaid enrollment data current.

documentation: Master compliance calendar
Report log (date, time, method, recipient, reporter)
Abuse Hotline confirmation numbers
Incident Reporting Form OP 3-0006 and follow-up reports
Census, capacity, evacuation and shelter reports
Regional Office notices for supervised-alternative DSPs and Corrective Action Plans
License renewal submission, sworn cost statement and closure notice copies

Proof of iConnect and Medicaid enrollment updates
